db-concurrency-control.title: Database Concurrency Control
db-concurrency-control.summary: Concurrency control techniques (locking 2PL, timestamp, optimistic, MVCC) that prevent anomalies in concurrent transactions, along with isolation levels and deadlock management.

requirements-specification.title: Technical Items of the Software Requirements Specification (SRS)
requirements-specification.summary: The items to be described in a requirements specification (overview, functional, non-functional, interface, constraints, data) and the quality attributes of good requirements.

data-governance.title: Data Governance
data-governance.summary: A control framework that integrally manages data standards, quality, metadata, security, and life cycle through policy, organization, process, and technology. Data stewardship and standardization are central, evolving toward data mesh, DataOps, and AI governance.

drone-security.title: Security Threats to Drones and Countermeasures
drone-security.summary: Drone threats such as GPS spoofing, communication hijacking, and firmware tampering, and countermeasures spanning communication, GPS, and firmware security, anti-drone, and regulation.

block-cipher.title: Block Cipher Algorithms
block-cipher.summary: Block ciphers (AES, DES) that repeatedly apply confusion and diffusion to plaintext in fixed block units, and operation modes ECB, CBC, CTR, and GCM.

6g.title: 6G Mobile Communication
6g.summary: The goals, core technologies, comparison with 5G, and standardization trends of 6G based on ITU-R IMT-2030 (Tbps, 0.1 ms, terrestrial-satellite integrated NTN, AI-native, integrated sensing and communication ISAC).

vxlan.title: VXLAN (Virtual eXtensible LAN)
vxlan.summary: A MAC-in-UDP tunneling technology that creates a 24-bit VNI-based L2 overlay over L3 to overcome the limitations of VLAN.

ml-optimization.title: Machine Learning Optimization Algorithms
ml-optimization.summary: The types, pros and cons of gradient-descent family algorithms (SGD, Momentum, AdaGrad, RMSProp, Adam) that minimize loss.

ismp.title: Information System Master Plan (ISMP)
ismp.summary: The stage-by-stage activities, details, and deliverables of ISMP, which plans the requirements of an individual information system project in detail before procurement.

ahp.title: AHP (Analytic Hierarchy Process)
ahp.summary: A multi-criteria decision-making technique that decomposes a problem into goal-criteria-alternative hierarchies and derives weights through pairwise comparison to select the optimal alternative.

bernoulli-geometric.title: Bernoulli Distribution and Geometric Distribution
bernoulli-geometric.summary: The definitions, expected values, variances, and memorylessness of the distributions for success/failure in a single trial (Bernoulli) and the number of trials until the first success (geometric), and their extension to the binomial and negative binomial distributions.

iso-21500.title: ISO 21500 (Guidance on Project Management)
iso-21500.summary: An international standard guide for project management composed of process groups (initiating, planning, implementing, controlling, closing) and subject groups.

data-mining-clustering.title: Data Mining: K-means, DBSCAN, SVM
data-mining-clustering.summary: The principles, parameters, and comparison of unsupervised clustering with K-means (centroid, distance) and DBSCAN (density) and supervised classification with SVM (maximum-margin hyperplane), along with practical selection criteria.

dsml-mlops.title: DSML Projects and MLOps
dsml-mlops.summary: The cyclical DSML project lifecycle (business → data → modeling → operations), and MLOps that versions data, models, and code while taming model decay through pipeline automation, monitoring, and continuous training (CT).

subnetting.title: Network Subnetting and Supernetting
subnetting.summary: Concepts of subnetting and supernetting, with a worked calculation of the mask (255.255.255.192) and assignable IPs (62) when dividing 192.168.100.0/24 into four subnets.

privacy-law-amendment.title: Amendment to the Personal Information Protection Act (2023)
privacy-law-amendment.summary: The 2023 amended Personal Information Protection Act: unified regulation, the right to data portability (the basis for MyData), the right to refuse and demand explanation of automated decisions, and stronger fines based on total revenue, plus data-processing actors and flows, a GDPR comparison, and corporate response strategies.

metaverse-ethics.title: Metaverse Ethics Principles
metaverse-ethics.summary: The metaverse ethics principles: three core values (an intact self, safe experience, sustainable prosperity), eight principles of practice, application procedures and shared responsibility, a comparison with internet and AI ethics, and immersive-data privacy.

digital-dysfunction.title: Digital Dysfunction
digital-dysfunction.summary: The concept and cases of digital dysfunction and its three key issues (overdependence, digital crime, digital divide), its intensification in the era of generative AI, and institutional, technical, educational, and social safety-net responses.

decision-tree.title: Decision Tree
decision-tree.summary: An interpretable model that builds a tree of if-then rules through repeated splitting on attribute criteria, covering information gain, Gini, overfitting, and ensembles.

file-db-blockchain.title: Data Storage: Files vs. DB vs. Blockchain
file-db-blockchain.summary: A comparison of files (application-managed), DBMS (centralized ACID), and blockchain (distributed-ledger immutability) in terms of trust authority, integrity, and performance.

tcp-congestion-control.title: TCP Congestion Control
tcp-congestion-control.summary: The TCP congestion control mechanism that regulates the congestion window (cwnd) through slow start, congestion avoidance, fast retransmit, and fast recovery.

ai-security-threats.title: AI Security Threats: Adversarial Attacks and Generative Vulnerabilities
ai-security-threats.summary: The four adversarial attacks on machine learning (poisoning, evasion, inversion, extraction) and their defenses, plus security vulnerabilities of generative LLMs and countermeasures.

bigdata-audit.title: Audit Checklist Items for Big Data Informatization Projects
bigdata-audit.summary: Checklist items for big data projects from the intelligent information technology audit guide, organized by analysis and design phase and by domain (data, analytical model, architecture, security).

financial-cloud-sla.title: Financial Cloud SLA
financial-cloud-sla.summary: The concept of an SLA and its key metrics (availability, RTO/RPO), and the differences between a general and a financial cloud SLA — domestic data residency, network separation, regulatory compliance, the shared responsibility model, BCP, and exit strategy.

voice-data-mining.title: Voice Data Mining
voice-data-mining.summary: A technique that exhaustively extracts information and patterns from unstructured voice via a pipeline of STT, speaker/emotion recognition, NLP, and pattern analysis — covering processing methods, application areas, the direction of generative AI advancement, and voice-data privacy challenges.

digital-forensics.title: Digital Forensics
digital-forensics.summary: The forensic science of collecting, analyzing, and preserving digital evidence while maintaining integrity and chain of custody — its concept, types, procedures, techniques, and applications.

cloud-security-considerations.title: Security Considerations When Adopting Cloud
cloud-security-considerations.summary: Under the premise of the shared responsibility model, reviewing data encryption and key management, IAM/CIEM, configuration security (CSPM), network and visibility, regulation (CSAP) and sovereignty, continuity and exit, and supply chain (SBOM). Misconfiguration and account management are the greatest risks, integrated through CNAPP and zero trust.

web3.title: Web 3.0
web3.summary: The concept of Web 3.0, which returns ownership of data and assets to users through blockchain-based decentralization, its technical elements (smart contracts, tokens, DID) and applications, and its limitations such as scalability and regulation.

dataops-devops.title: DataOps and DevOps
dataops-devops.summary: A comparison of DevOps, which automates code deployment, and DataOps, which automates data pipelines and analytics, along with DataOps architecture and technologies.

digital-platform-gov.title: Digital Platform Government
digital-platform-gov.summary: A paradigm that integrates and opens government data and services on a single platform to deliver proactive, personalized administration and public-private co-creation of value — its four-layer structure, a comparison with e-government, and the balance between standards and governance and privacy protection.

ai-ethics-standard.title: AI Ethics Standards: Three Principles and Ten Requirements
ai-ethics-standard.summary: Under the overarching principle of humanity in the national AI ethics standards (Dec 2020), the three basic principles (human dignity, the common good, purposiveness) and the ten core requirements. The shift from voluntary norms to the AI Basic Act (effective Jan 2026) and embedding ethics at the design stage.

aop.title: AOP (Aspect-Oriented Programming)
aop.summary: A paradigm that separates cross-cutting concerns such as logging, security, and transactions into aspects and stitches them in through weaving. Covers its components, types of advice and weaving, application in Spring, and extension to service mesh.

transaction-acid.title: Characteristics of Database Transactions (ACID)
transaction-acid.summary: The atomicity, consistency, isolation, and durability (ACID) of transactions and their implementation techniques (locking, MVCC, WAL), isolation levels, and extensions to CAP, BASE, 2PC, and Saga in distributed environments.

coupling.title: Types of Software Coupling
coupling.summary: The types of coupling that weaken in the order content > common > external > control > stamp > data, and the design principles of low coupling and high cohesion.

iac.title: Infrastructure as Code (IaC)
iac.summary: An approach that declares infrastructure's desired state as code for automated provisioning and management. Encompassing declarative and imperative styles, idempotency, state management, and security (secrets, Policy as Code), it forms the foundation of cloud-native operations, extending to DevOps and GitOps.

security-product-fast-cert.title: Fast-Track Verification Scheme for Information Security Products
security-product-fast-cert.summary: A scheme that rapidly verifies the security of new-technology and converged security products whose adoption was blocked by the absence of evaluation criteria, thereby supporting their public-sector adoption.

noma.title: Non-Orthogonal Multiple Access (NOMA)
noma.summary: The principles of NOMA, which superimposes and shares the same time and frequency by power difference and separates signals with SIC, its core technologies (power allocation, superposition coding, SIC), a comparison with OMA, and application to 5G/6G hyper-connectivity.

tree-sort.title: Tree Sort
tree-sort.summary: An algorithm that sorts by inserting into a binary search tree and then performing an in-order traversal. Covers its principle and complexity (average O(n log n), O(n²) when skewed), avoiding the worst case with balanced trees such as AVL and red-black, and applications to dynamic data.

virtualization.title: Virtualization
virtualization.summary: Virtualization, which logically abstracts physical resources — server virtualization (hypervisor), application virtualization, VDI, and containers; the VM/container trade-off; and the foundation of cloud and cloud-native.

agile-scrum-kanban.title: Structured Methodology and Agile (Scrum and Kanban)
agile-scrum-kanban.summary: A comparison of structured methodology and Agile, the Agile implementations Scrum (time-boxing) and Kanban (flow optimization), and approaches to executing them effectively.

refactoring.title: Refactoring and Design Patterns
refactoring.summary: Refactoring, which improves structure while preserving behavior, and design patterns, which are proven design solutions — their definitions, techniques, code smells, and commonalities and differences.

deepview.title: DeepView
deepview.summary: DeepView, a deep-learning-based intelligent video content analysis (VCA) technology — its concept and processing pipeline (object detection, tracking/re-identification, behavior analysis, intelligent search), use cases, and advanced challenges such as edge AI, privacy, and bias.

large-scale-system-failure.title: Post-Launch Problems and Countermeasures for Large-Scale Public Next-Generation Systems
large-scale-system-failure.summary: The causes of failures after launching large-scale public systems, countermeasures and legal/institutional improvements to prevent recurrence, and indicator management for judging launch readiness.

wbs.title: Work Breakdown Structure (WBS)
wbs.summary: The WBS, which decomposes project scope hierarchically down to work packages around deliverables — its components, authoring principles (100% rule, MECE, 8/80), linkage with other plans (EVM, RAM), agile variants, and measures to recover schedule delays.

text-opinion-mining.title: Data Mining: Difference from Statistics, Structured/Unstructured, Opinion/Text
text-opinion-mining.summary: The difference between data mining and statistics, a comparison of structured and unstructured mining, and the opinion mining process versus text mining.

event-driven-architecture.title: Event-Driven Architecture (EDA) Topologies
event-driven-architecture.summary: A comparison of the mediator and broker topologies of EDA, which loosely couples components through event publishing and subscription, its components, and extensions to Saga, eventual consistency, event sourcing, and CQRS.

infostealer.title: InfoStealer
infostealer.summary: Information-stealing malware that covertly exfiltrates sensitive data such as accounts, session cookies, and cryptocurrency wallets. Its attack procedure (kill chain) and the MaaS crime ecosystem, MFA bypass via session cookies, and a layered response of prevention, stronger authentication, EDR detection, and dark-web monitoring.

db-normalization.title: Database Normalization
db-normalization.summary: Normalization to eliminate redundancy and prevent anomalies (insertion, deletion, update) — how anomalies arise, lossless decomposition based on functional dependencies, the stages from 1NF to BCNF, and the trade-off with denormalization.

semiconductor-industry.title: The Semiconductor Industry (Memory, Non-Memory, Value Chain)
semiconductor-industry.summary: A comparison of memory and non-memory semiconductors, the design-manufacturing-packaging value chain, and strategies such as fostering fabless companies to grow the non-memory sector.

it-investment-analysis.title: IT Investment Analysis (Process, Framework, Methodology)
it-investment-analysis.summary: The process, frameworks (BSC, portfolio), and methodologies (NPV, ROI, AHP) for evaluating the business value of IT investment, and the balance between qualitative and quantitative approaches.

it-roi.title: IT-ROI Investment Performance Evaluation Model
it-roi.summary: The IT-ROI model that quantitatively evaluates benefits against IT investment cost (TCO), its tangible and intangible benefits, and linkage with information economics and BSC.

pop.title: POP (Point of Production)
pop.summary: POP, which collects shop-floor information in real time at the point and place of occurrence — its structure and collected information, linkage with MES and ERP, a comparison with POS and MES, and its evolution toward the smart factory through OPC-UA and predictive maintenance.

model-ops.title: Machine Learning Modeling and ModelOps
model-ops.summary: The difference between modeling, which develops models, and ModelOps, which continuously manages models as trusted assets through deployment, monitoring, retraining (CT), and governance — their architecture, maturity, and extension to LLMOps.

quality-cost.title: Software Cost of Quality
quality-cost.summary: The four cost-of-quality categories of conformance cost (prevention, appraisal) and non-conformance cost (internal, external failure) and their trade-off relationship. Covers the law of escalating defect-fix cost, the optimal investment point, and Shift-Left/Right in depth.

cbam.title: CBAM (Cost Benefit Analysis Method)
cbam.summary: An architecture evaluation method (an extension of ATAM) that analyzes the costs and benefits of architectural strategies to set ROI-based investment priorities.

correlation-causation.title: Correlation and Causation
correlation-causation.summary: A comparison of correlation, where things vary together, and causation, a cause-and-effect relationship; the pitfall that correlation ≠ causation; and verification through experiments and causal inference.

neuromorphic.title: Neuromorphic Chip
neuromorphic.summary: A brain-inspired semiconductor that mimics the brain's neurons and synapses to integrate computation and memory and operate via spikes, enabling low-power edge AI.

memory-interleaving.title: Memory Interleaving
memory-interleaving.summary: A technique that divides memory into multiple banks and channels and distributes consecutive addresses across them to raise bandwidth through parallel, overlapped access. Covers low-/high-order interleaving, bank conflicts, the relationship with cache, and extension to HBM and NUMA.

ransomware-raas.title: Ransomware and RaaS
ransomware-raas.summary: Ransomware, which encrypts and steals data to demand a ransom, and RaaS, an as-a-service model with a division of labor among developers, affiliates, and IABs. Responding to the evolution into double and triple extortion with immutable backups (3-2-1), EDR/XDR, least privilege, and IR.

qubit.title: Qubit
qubit.summary: The qubit as a unit of quantum information that represents 2^n states simultaneously via superposition and entanglement of 0 and 1: its principles, implementation, decoherence, and cryptographic threats.

public-private-cloud.title: Use of Private-Sector Cloud in the Public Sector
public-private-cloud.summary: Procedures and baseline design for public-sector adoption of private-sector cloud, its usage architecture and CSAP certification, and evaluation criteria by SaaS/PaaS/IaaS type.

scm.title: Supply Chain Management (SCM)
scm.summary: The concept and background of SCM, which integrates and optimizes the flow of materials, information, and funds across the procurement-production-distribution-consumption supply chain; causes and mitigation of the bullwhip effect (VMI, CPFR); demand forecasting and safety-stock calculation; and digital SCM and resilience.

digital-transformation-coe.title: Digital Transformation and the CoE (Center of Excellence)
digital-transformation-coe.summary: Considerations for successful digital transformation (vision, data, culture, talent) and the role of the CoE in consolidating and disseminating capabilities.

inductive-ml.title: Inductive Reasoning and Machine Learning
inductive-ml.summary: The correspondence between inductive reasoning, which generalizes rules from individual cases, and machine learning that automates it; hypothesis space and inductive bias; the limits of generalization error and data bias; and complements such as neuro-symbolic AI, RAG, and XAI.

data3law-mydata.title: The Three Data Acts and MyData
data3law-mydata.summary: The amendment of the Three Data Acts, which introduced pseudonymized data and unified oversight to balance protection and utilization, and the concept of MyData based on the right to data portability and standardized APIs, including information provided by industry, cross-sector expansion, and promotion measures.

module-cohesion-coupling.title: Software Modules — Cohesion, Coupling, and Fan-in/out
module-cohesion-coupling.summary: Cohesion and coupling as measures of module design (high cohesion, low coupling), and the Fan-in (reuse) and Fan-out (dependency) metrics.

web-performance.title: Web Performance Management and Front-End Optimization
web-performance.summary: Factors that degrade web performance and front-end optimization measures such as resource compression, image optimization, request reduction, caching, and rendering optimization.

stpa.title: STPA (System-Theoretic Process Analysis)
stpa.summary: The limits of component-failure-centric FMEA and HAZOP, and the concept and method of STPA, a systems-theory-based approach that analyzes control and interaction errors.

public-sw-planning.title: Public SW Project Planning-Stage Review and Adequacy of Scope Changes
public-sw-planning.summary: Review items for the finalization and duration adequacy of public SW projects, and the criteria for judging the adequacy of scope changes during project execution.

data-migration.title: Data Integration and Migration — Integrity and Consistency
data-migration.summary: The difference between integrity and consistency in data migration, profiling-analysis perspectives, multi-layered verification methods, and rehearsal, rollback, and CDC cutover strategies.

federated-learning.title: Federated Learning
federated-learning.summary: The operating principles and algorithm (FedAvg) of federated learning, which aggregates only locally trained models without gathering the data, and its security and privacy technologies.

nft-security.title: Characteristics and Security Vulnerabilities of NFT Marketplaces
nft-security.summary: The characteristics of NFTs (irreversibility, off-chain storage) and the security vulnerabilities of NFT marketplaces (phishing signature theft, contract flaws) and their countermeasures.

reverse-proxy-ddos.title: Web Server Security — Reverse Proxy and DDoS Cyber Shelter
reverse-proxy-ddos.summary: The reverse proxy that protects the front end of a web server (concealment, load balancing, SSL, WAF) and the cyber shelter for responding to large-scale DDoS (rerouting, scrubbing), with CDN-integrated multi-layered defense.

satin.title: SATIN (Satellite-Aerial-Terrestrial Integrated Network)
satin.summary: SATIN, a 6G-oriented three-dimensional wireless network that integrates satellite (wide-area), aerial (drones, HAPS), and terrestrial (high-capacity) layers into a single control plane: roles by layer, handover, integration technologies, applications in disaster response, UAVs, and remote areas, and spectrum and security challenges.

quantum-crypto.title: Quantum Cryptography
quantum-crypto.summary: The methods, technologies, and vulnerabilities of quantum cryptography (QKD), which detects eavesdropping and distributes keys using the quantum-mechanical principles of measurement disturbance and no-cloning.

identification-authentication.title: Identification and Authentication
identification-authentication.summary: The difference between identification, which claims an identity, and authentication, which verifies its authenticity (identification → authentication → authorization → audit); security requirements; the four authentication factors of knowledge, possession, biometrics, and behavior; and MFA, passkeys (FIDO2), and adaptive authentication.

nft.title: Non-Fungible Token (NFT)
nft.summary: The structure, standards (ERC-721/1155), and issuance/trading of NFTs, which use blockchain smart contracts to prove the uniqueness and ownership of digital and physical assets, along with RWA applications and challenges of off-chain persistence, copyright, speculation, and regulation.

bsc.title: Balanced Scorecard (BSC)
bsc.summary: The components and strategy map of the BSC, which measures performance in a balanced way across the four perspectives of financial, customer, internal process, and learning and growth.

mac.title: Message Authentication Code (MAC)
mac.summary: A symmetric-key technique that verifies integrity and origin authentication by generating a keyed authentication tag from a message and a shared secret key and comparing it upon recomputation. Covers HMAC/CMAC/GMAC types, the non-repudiation difference from digital signatures, and the evolution toward AEAD.

spring-boot.title: Spring Boot
spring-boot.summary: The characteristics of Spring Boot, which rapidly develops standalone applications with minimal configuration through auto-configuration, starters, and an embedded server.

test-code-coverage.title: Test Coverage and Code Coverage
test-code-coverage.summary: The relationship and comparison between test coverage, which validates requirements, functions, and risks, and code coverage, which instruments code execution (statement, branch, condition, MC/DC). Covers the limits of 100% coverage and mutation testing, CI quality gates, and risk-based target setting.

mongodb.title: MongoDB
mongodb.summary: The data model, replica sets, sharding, indexes, and aggregation of MongoDB, a document-oriented NoSQL database that stores data as JSON-like documents (BSON); its comparison with relational databases; and recent trends such as transactions and vector search.

modification-fabrication.title: Modification and Fabrication
modification-fabrication.summary: Modification is the illegal alteration of an original (integrity violation), while fabrication is the false creation or impersonation of something that did not exist (integrity plus authentication violation); these are countered with hashes and MACs (modification detection) and digital signatures and PKI (fabrication prevention, authentication, non-repudiation), extending in the AI era to deepfakes and C2PA provenance proof.

overfitting.title: Overfitting
overfitting.summary: The causes of overfitting (complexity, insufficient data, noise, over-training) and remedies such as regularization, dropout, early stopping, and cross-validation, with an in-depth look at the bias-variance trade-off.

digital-twin-metaverse.title: Digital Twin and Metaverse
digital-twin-metaverse.summary: A comparison of the digital twin, which replicates and predicts reality, with the metaverse for virtual experience and communication, and their convergence in the industrial metaverse.

daas.title: DaaS (Desktop as a Service)
daas.summary: The architecture of DaaS, which delivers desktop environments virtually from the cloud, its comparison with VDI, and its strengths in mobility, security, and centralized management.

egov-evaluation.title: UN E-Government Survey
egov-evaluation.summary: The concept and indices of the UN E-Government Survey (the E-Government Development Index EGDI and the E-Participation Index) and the derivation of EGDI from online services, telecommunication infrastructure, and human capital.

db-tuning.title: Database Tuning
db-tuning.summary: The concept and purpose of tuning, which diagnoses and optimizes database performance degradation based on execution plans, and techniques by layer: design (denormalization, indexing, partitioning), DBMS, and SQL (optimizer, hints).

on-device-ai.title: On-Device AI
on-device-ai.summary: The concept of on-device AI, which performs AI inference directly on the device, its HW/SW technologies (NPU, model compression), and a comparison with cloud AI.

access-control-model.title: Access Control Security Models (BLP, Biba, Clark-Wilson)
access-control-model.summary: A comparison of BLP for confidentiality (No Read-Up, No Write-Down), Biba for integrity (No Write-Up, No Read-Down), and Clark-Wilson for commercial integrity (transactions, separation of duties) as symmetries in the direction of threat.

master-data-management.title: Master Data Management (MDM)
master-data-management.summary: The concept and necessity of MDM, which manages core reference data such as customers and products in a single, unified way, its components, and considerations during implementation.

db-optimizer.title: Database Optimizer (RBO, CBO)
db-optimizer.summary: The concept of the optimizer, which selects the optimal execution plan for SQL, a comparison of the rule-based RBO (deprecated) and the cost-based CBO (standard), tuning factors such as statistics, histograms, and hints, and adaptive optimization.

sdn.title: Software-Defined Networking (SDN)
sdn.summary: The three-tier architecture and control-plane characteristics of SDN, which separates the control plane from the data plane so that a central controller exercises global control, the OpenFlow operating procedure, and the evolution toward NFV and intent-based networking.

soar.title: SOAR (Security Orchestration, Automation, and Response)
soar.summary: SOAR, which integrates security operations into orchestration, automation, and response: reducing response time (MTTR) through playbook automation, complementing SIEM (detection), and evolving into an AI-integrated autonomous SOC.

msa.title: Microservices Architecture (MSA)
msa.summary: An architecture that decomposes an application into small, independently deployable and scalable services. Covers a comparison with monoliths, saga and circuit breaker, service mesh (Istio), DDD-based decomposition, and Kubernetes and incremental migration.

data-commerce.title: Data Commerce
data-commerce.summary: Data-driven commerce that uses AI to analyze customer data and recommends and sells personalized products and services at the right time.

db-sharding.title: Database Sharding
db-sharding.summary: A technique that horizontally partitions large volumes of data across multiple DB servers to achieve load balancing and scalability. Covers a comparison with partitioning and the shard key.

data-industry-act.title: Data Industry Act (Data Industry Promotion Act)
data-industry-act.summary: A framework act that promotes the data industry by facilitating the production, trading, and utilization of data. Covers data asset protection, valuation, and trade facilitation.

uml-sequence.title: UML Sequence Diagram
uml-sequence.summary: A UML dynamic diagram that represents messages between objects in chronological order. Covers lifelines, activation boxes, messages, frames, and guards.

normal-distribution.title: Characteristics of the Normal Distribution
normal-distribution.summary: A continuous, bell-shaped distribution symmetric about its mean. As a foundation of statistical inference through the 68-95-99.7 rule, standardization (Z), and the central limit theorem, it also addresses fat-tail risk and normality testing.

metaheuristics.title: Metaheuristics
metaheuristics.summary: General-purpose search strategies that find good approximate solutions to large-scale optimization problems in practical time. Includes genetic, simulated annealing, ant colony, and particle swarm methods.

race-condition.title: Race Condition
race-condition.summary: A non-deterministic error in which the result varies with execution order due to unprotected concurrent access to a shared resource. Covers critical sections and mutual exclusion (mutex, semaphore, CAS), and control of deadlock and TOCTOU.

snn.title: Spiking Neural Network (SNN)
snn.summary: A third-generation, event-driven neural network that mimics neuronal spike firing and firing timing (temporal information). It computes only when a spike occurs, achieving ultra-low power and low latency; because backpropagation is hard to apply, it advances alongside dedicated training methods such as surrogate gradients, STDP, and ANN conversion, and neuromorphic hardware.

bigdata-analysis-tools.title: Principles for Selecting Big Data Analysis Tools
bigdata-analysis-tools.summary: Principles for choosing a tool combination suited to the situation by comprehensively considering analysis purpose → data characteristics → scalability and performance → TCO, workforce competency, and governance. Also reflects the shift to cloud-managed services and the lakehouse.

software-quality-certification.title: Software Quality Certification (GS Certification)
software-quality-certification.summary: A scheme in which a third party tests and certifies the quality of SW products based on ISO/IEC 25000. Covers resolving information asymmetry and preferential treatment in public procurement.

pacelc.title: Limits of the CAP Theorem and PACELC
pacelc.summary: CAP only explains the C-vs-A choice during a partition. PACELC adds the latency (L) vs. consistency (C) trade-off under normal operation to guide distributed DB selection.

embedded-software-test.title: Embedded Software Testing
embedded-software-test.summary: Closed-loop verification covering hardware, real-time behavior, resource constraints, and safety. The MIL to SIL to PIL to HIL stages, with MC/DC coverage per ISO 26262 and DO-178C.

thrashing.title: Thrashing
thrashing.summary: Excessive multiprogramming causes page faults to surge so the CPU does little but swap, and performance collapses. Working set and PFF.

endianness.title: Big-Endian and Little-Endian
endianness.summary: The byte order for storing multibyte data. Big (MSB first, the network standard) vs. little (LSB first, x86), and conversion in heterogeneous communication.

network-scanning.title: Network Scanning
network-scanning.summary: Active probing of hosts, ports, services, and vulnerabilities, serving both as attack reconnaissance and defensive assessment. SYN, FIN, UDP and other techniques that abuse the 3-way handshake, with attack-surface minimization and IDS/IPS and SIEM/SOAR integration.

file-slack.title: File Slack
file-slack.summary: The space left over when a file does not fully fill a cluster. RAM and drive slack, where deleted data persists and is exploited as forensic evidence or for concealment.

sw-cost-estimation.title: Software Cost Estimation Methods
sw-cost-estimation.summary: A risk-management activity that predicts effort, schedule, and cost before project kickoff. The trade-offs among top-down (expert, Delphi), bottom-up (WBS), and mathematical models (COCOMO, Function Point), Korea's Function Point standard (2024 FP unit price KRW 605,784), and Agile and AI-based estimation.

digital-tax.title: Digital Tax
digital-tax.summary: An OECD/G20 international tax framework letting market jurisdictions also tax Big Tech that earns cross-border revenue without a physical presence. Reallocation of taxing rights (Pillar 1), the 15% global minimum tax (Pillar 2), the BEPS response, the US withdrawal, and recent Side-by-Side developments.

uml-class-diagram.title: UML Class Diagrams and Object Modeling
uml-class-diagram.summary: A static model expressing classes with their attributes, operations, and relationships (association, aggregation, composition, generalization). The design convergence point running from conceptual objects to sequences (message to method) to classes, with two-way linkage to code.

blockchain-types.title: Blockchain Types (Public, Private, Hybrid)
blockchain-types.summary: Classifying blockchains by openness into public (open, decentralized), private (permissioned, controlled), consortium, and hybrid. Trade-offs from the perspective of consensus and the trilemma, with regulatory and interoperability considerations.

bigdata-platform-architecture.title: Big Data Platform Architecture Design
bigdata-platform-architecture.summary: A scalable layered structure supporting ingestion, storage, processing, and analysis. Distributed infrastructure, data lake/warehouse/lakehouse, batch and real-time (Lambda/Kappa), and evolution toward MLOps.

db-standardization-guideline.title: Public-Sector DB Standardization Guidelines: Table Definition Document
db-standardization-guideline.summary: A deliverable that documents table structure, meaning, and constraints in a standard format per the standardization guidelines. Recorded items, authoring guidance, quality diagnosis, and linkage to data governance are covered in depth.

web-quality-standard.title: E-Government Website Quality (Accessibility, Compatibility, Openness, Optimization)
web-quality-standard.summary: UI/UX design criteria plus web accessibility, compatibility, openness, and optimization to guarantee all citizens equal, non-discriminatory use. KWCAG-based accessibility is a legal obligation.

software-safety-diagnosis.title: SW Safety Diagnosis: Functional-Behavior Correctness Diagnosis
software-safety-diagnosis.summary: Traceability-based verification of correctness at each stage: requirements, design, implementation, and test. Includes normal, abnormal, and boundary conditions, linked to functional-safety standards such as ISO 26262 and IEC 61508.

ensemble-learning.title: Ensemble Learning: Bagging and Boosting
ensemble-learning.summary: Techniques that combine multiple weak learners into a strong model. Bagging (parallel, lowers variance) and boosting (sequential, lowers bias) are complementary.

software-architecture-analysis.title: Software Architecture Analysis and ATAM
software-architecture-analysis.summary: Evaluating whether a structure satisfies quality-attribute requirements. ATAM uses quality scenarios to elicit sensitivity points, trade-offs, and risks.

metaverse-security.title: Metaverse Security Threats and Social Issues
metaverse-security.summary: Threats arising from immersion, avatars, and the virtual economy such as biometric leakage, account/asset theft, and impersonation, alongside identity confusion, virtual violence, and addiction, with technical, institutional, and ethical measures.

priority-inversion.title: Priority Inversion
priority-inversion.summary: A phenomenon where a high-priority task runs late because a low-priority task holds a resource and a medium-priority task preempts it. Resolved by priority inheritance and priority ceiling.

mirai-botnet.title: Mirai Botnet
mirai-botnet.summary: A botnet that mass-infected IoT devices left with default Telnet passwords via dictionary attacks and abused them for large-scale DDoS. The infection chain, security across the lifecycle, the 7 common security principles, and the variants and regulatory trends after the source code was released.

tor.title: Tor vs. VPN
tor.summary: An anonymity network that hides identity through multi-node onion routing. Compared with the single-server trust of a VPN in terms of trust model, speed, and purpose.

rsa-dsa.title: RSA vs. DSA
rsa-dsa.summary: Comparing factorization-based, general-purpose RSA (encryption and signing) with discrete-logarithm-based, signing-only DSA. Signature generation/verification speed, and the evolution to ECDSA and PQC.

file-carving.title: File Carving
file-carving.summary: Recovering files from raw data by their signatures and structure without file-system metadata. The four techniques (header/footer, structure, content, defragmentation) and handling of integrity and SSD TRIM.

secaas.title: SECaaS (Security as a Service)
secaas.summary: A model delivering security functions as a cloud subscription service. It provides up-to-date, expert security and collective defense with no upfront investment, while managing shared responsibility, SLAs, data sovereignty, and lock-in, and evolving toward Zero Trust-based SASE/SSE.

java-awt-swing.title: Java AWT and Swing
java-awt-swing.summary: Comparing heavyweight OS-native-dependent GUI (AWT) with lightweight, Java-rendered GUI (Swing). Platform independence, look-and-feel, and the evolution to JavaFX.

mece.title: MECE (Mutually Exclusive, Collectively Exhaustive)
mece.summary: A classification principle where items do not overlap (ME) and cover the whole without gaps (CE). Removing overlap and omission for accurate analysis, using the logic tree.

post-quantum-crypto.title: Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC)
post-quantum-crypto.summary: Quantum-resistant public-key cryptography based on lattices, hashes, and codes that remains hard even for quantum computers (Shor's algorithm). The urgency of migration seen through Harvest-Now-Decrypt-Later (HNDL) and Mosca's inequality, the NIST standards (ML-KEM, ML-DSA, SLH-DSA), and hybrid mode and crypto-agility.

wfq.title: WFQ (Weighted Fair Queuing)
wfq.summary: A queuing scheme that approximates GPS per packet (PGPS), assigns weights to traffic flows, and allocates bandwidth byte-fairly in order of virtual finish time. It solves FIFO monopoly, PQ starvation, and WRR size-unfairness, with CBWFQ, LLQ, and DRR extensions.

sdr.title: SDR (Software Defined Radio)
sdr.summary: Implementing radio signal processing (modulation/demodulation, filtering, protocols) in software so one device supports multiple standards and frequencies. Early digitization and software processing provide flexibility and scalability, forming the basis for 5G/6G software-defined infrastructure such as cognitive radio, Open RAN, and satellite (NTN).

earned-value-management.title: Earned Value Management (EVM)
earned-value-management.summary: Integrated measurement of schedule and cost performance via PV, EV, and AC. SV/CV/SPI/CPI analysis, worked calculations, and crashing and fast tracking in response to schedule-delay threats.

interconnection-network.title: Parallel-Processing Interconnection Networks and the Torus
interconnection-network.summary: The communication structure connecting processors and memory that governs parallel performance. Bus, crossbar, mesh, and hypercube; the torus shortens distance and provides symmetric distribution by connecting the mesh edges.

emp-attack.title: EMP Attack (ElectroMagnetic Pulse)
emp-attack.summary: A threat that physically destroys electronic, power, and communication hardware with a powerful electromagnetic pulse. The E1/E2/E3 components of a high-altitude nuclear HEMP, layered defense through shielding, grounding, and filtering, and resilience strategies with isolated spares and redundancy.

qos-diffserv-intserv.title: QoS: DiffServ and IntServ
qos-diffserv-intserv.summary: Architectures that guarantee network service quality. Comparing IntServ (per-flow RSVP reservation, hard guarantee, low scalability) with DiffServ (DSCP/PHB class differentiation, stateless, high scalability), with WFQ/WRED queuing linkage and SDN and 5G slicing trends.

ai-privacy-checklist.title: AI Personal Data Protection Self-Assessment Checklist
ai-privacy-checklist.summary: A voluntary code by which operators self-check that they process personal data lawfully and safely across the entire AI lifecycle. The principles of lawfulness, safety, transparency, and rights protection.

jwt.title: JWT (JSON Web Token)
jwt.summary: A stateless token that carries and signs authentication information. The Header, Payload, and Signature structure, its fit for MSA and API authentication, and mitigations for payload exposure and revocation limits.

shannon-theory.title: Information Theory and Shannon's Theorems
shannon-theory.summary: Quantifying information as entropy. The first theorem (compression limit = entropy), the second theorem (zero error within capacity), and Shannon-Hartley (C = B*log2(1+S/N)), extended to AI.

dag-topological-sort.title: Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG) and Topological Sort
dag-topological-sort.summary: A directed, cycle-free graph expressing precedence and dependency. Topological sort (Kahn: remove nodes with in-degree 0 first) determines build and scheduling order.

procedural-vs-oop.title: Procedural and Object-Oriented Programming
procedural-vs-oop.summary: Comparing procedural programming centered on function flow with object-oriented programming that encapsulates data and behavior into objects. Inheritance and polymorphism make it well suited to large-scale systems.

purdue-model.title: Industrial Control System (ICS) Purdue Model
purdue-model.summary: A reference architecture dividing an ICS into layers from physical process (L0) to enterprise IT (L4-5). An IT/OT DMZ isolates the layers to block threat propagation.

oauth2-oidc.title: OAuth 2.0 and OpenID Connect (OIDC)
oauth2-oidc.summary: OAuth 2.0 is an authorization framework that delegates limited permissions without exposing passwords; OIDC is an authentication layer atop it that proves identity with a signed ID token, including the latest security-hardening standards such as PKCE, FAPI, and OAuth 2.1.

service-mesh.title: Service Mesh
service-mesh.summary: Organizes the architecture and adoption strategy of a service mesh, which splits inter-microservice communication into a data plane and control plane to deliver traffic management, reliability, mTLS security, and observability consistently.

finops.title: FinOps (Cloud Cost and Value Optimization)
finops.summary: Studies the FinOps framework, which connects cost to business value through visibility, allocation, optimization, and operation of cloud and technology spend.

cqrs-event-sourcing.title: CQRS and Event Sourcing (Command Query Responsibility Segregation, Event Sourcing)
cqrs-event-sourcing.summary: Organizes the principles of CQRS, which separates read and write responsibilities, and event sourcing, which preserves change history as events, along with their combined structure, consistency, reprocessing, schema evolution, and adoption strategy.

slo-error-budget.title: Service Reliability Management Based on SLO, SLI, and Error Budget
slo-error-budget.summary: Organizes how to measure service levels from the user's perspective with SLIs and SLOs and connect the error budget to decisions on deployment, incident response, and reliability investment.

chaos-engineering.title: Fault-Tolerance Verification Based on Chaos Engineering
chaos-engineering.summary: Organizes an experimental framework that uses controlled fault injection and steady-state hypotheses to verify and improve the fault tolerance, recovery automation, and observability of distributed systems.

circuit-breaker.title: Circuit Breaker Pattern and Fault Isolation
circuit-breaker.summary: Explains the circuit breaker's state model, which detects failures and delays in remote dependencies to block calls and confirms recovery with limited trial calls, along with its combination of retries and timeouts, fallback, and operational design.

data-lakehouse.title: Data Lakehouse Architecture and Governance
data-lakehouse.summary: Organizes an architecture that combines the scalability and openness of a data lake with the consistency and manageability of a data warehouse, integrating Bronze, Silver, and Gold data products with ACID, schema, quality, lineage, and privacy governance.

api-gateway.title: API Gateway Architecture and Operations
api-gateway.summary: An essay-style overview of the architecture, design, and operational strategy of the API gateway, which unifies routing, authentication and authorization, traffic control, and observability between clients and backend services.

domain-driven-design.title: Domain-Driven Design (DDD)
domain-driven-design.summary: A method of reflecting the core concepts and rules of a complex business domain in the software model and designing systems resilient to change through bounded contexts and tactical patterns.

observability.title: Observability and OpenTelemetry
observability.summary: The system property of correlating the three signals—metrics, logs, and traces—via trace IDs to investigate even unknown failures after the fact, together with OpenTelemetry standard instrumentation, sampling, and cardinality governance strategies.

serverless-computing.title: Serverless Computing (Serverless / FaaS)
serverless-computing.summary: A model that delegates infrastructure operations to the provider and runs event-driven stateless functions (FaaS) and managed backends (BaaS) with usage-based billing and scale-to-zero—weighing cold-start, execution-constraint, and vendor lock-in trade-offs against workload characteristics.

vector-database.title: Vector Database
vector-database.summary: A database that performs high-speed similarity search over high-dimensional vectors—embeddings of unstructured data—using ANN indexes. With HNSW, IVF, and PQ indexes plus hybrid search and re-ranking, it serves as a semantic knowledge store for RAG, recommendation, and anomaly detection, where balancing the accuracy–performance–cost trade-off is key.

saga-pattern.title: Saga Pattern and Distributed Transactions
saga-pattern.summary: A distributed-transaction technique that splits a transaction spanning multiple services into a chain of local transactions and, on failure, undoes them in reverse order via compensating transactions to achieve atomicity at the application level—an eventual-consistency strategy that trades 2PC's strong consistency for availability and scalability, where the choice between choreography and orchestration and the design of idempotency, outbox, and compensation determine success or failure.

passkey-fido2.title: Passkeys and FIDO2/WebAuthn
passkey-fido2.summary: Passwordless authentication based on FIDO2 (WebAuthn + CTAP) that keeps the private key in the device's secure enclave and logs in with domain-bound public-key signatures, fundamentally blocking phishing, credential stuffing, and server breaches. By eliminating shared secrets and preventing phishing through origin binding, the choice between synced and device-bound types and the design of the account-recovery path govern the security–convenience trade-off.

distributed-consensus.title: Distributed Consensus Algorithms — Paxos and Raft
distributed-consensus.summary: A technique by which multiple nodes agree on the same command order through majority quorum and log replication under partial failures—covering the principles of Paxos and Raft, leader election, safety, and practical adoption in systems such as etcd.

data-mesh.title: Data Mesh and Distributed Data Architecture
data-mesh.summary: A socio-technical distributed data architecture that decentralizes ownership of analytical data from a central data team to business domains, treats data as a discoverable, trustworthy product (Data as a Product), and maintains interoperability through a self-service platform and policy-as-code federated governance—delving into its four principles, its differences from the lakehouse and data fabric, and incremental adoption strategies.

change-data-capture.title: Change Data Capture (CDC)
change-data-capture.summary: A data-integration technique that extracts only changes (INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE) in real time from sources such as a source DB's transaction log and propagates them downstream—covering log-, trigger-, and query-based approaches and offset, ordering, idempotency, and outbox patterns.

graphql.title: GraphQL (API Query Language)
graphql.summary: An API specification in which clients select only the fields they need within a strongly typed schema and query a single endpoint—resolving over-/under-fetching and covering resolvers, the N+1 problem, DataLoader, comparison with REST, and caching, security, and federation.

sase.title: SASE (Secure Access Service Edge)
sase.summary: An architecture that converges SD-WAN (connectivity) with SWG, CASB, ZTNA, and FWaaS (security = SSE) at the cloud edge in an identity-centric, single-pass model—delivering performance by eliminating backhaul and securing perimeterless environments through zero trust.

quic-http3.title: QUIC and HTTP/3
quic-http3.summary: QUIC, which integrates TLS 1.3, stream multiplexing, and reliability over UDP to eliminate transport-layer head-of-line blocking and enable 0-RTT connections and connection migration, and HTTP/3, the next-generation web protocol built on it.

confidential-computing.title: Confidential Computing
confidential-computing.summary: A hardware-isolated data-protection paradigm that uses a CPU hardware-based trusted execution environment (TEE) and remote attestation to protect data even while it is 'in use' during computation, excluding even the hypervisor and cloud operator from the trust boundary.

devsecops.title: DevSecOps
devsecops.summary: An integrated development-security-operations methodology that embeds security across the entire SDLC through automation (Security as Code) and shifts it left, achieving fast deployment and safety at the same time—covering SAST, DAST, IAST, SCA, and pipeline gates.

grpc.title: gRPC (Google RPC Framework)
grpc.summary: An RPC framework that combines Protocol Buffers' strongly typed contracts and code generation, binary serialization, and HTTP/2 multiplexing and streaming to deliver low-latency, high-throughput communication between microservices—a pillar of a tiered API strategy that uses gRPC internally and REST/GraphQL externally.

aiops.title: AIOps (Intelligent IT Operations)
aiops.summary: An approach that applies big data and machine learning to IT operations to make anomaly detection, alert correlation, root-cause analysis (RCA), prediction, and automated response intelligent—shifting reactive operations to a predictive, autonomous model and shortening MTTR, where data quality and the design of phased automation and safeguards determine success or failure.

transformer-attention.title: Transformers and the Attention Mechanism
transformer-attention.summary: An architecture that, without recurrence or convolution, computes relationships across an entire sequence in parallel using only Query-Key-Value self-attention, achieving long-range dependency modeling and scalability—covering multi-head attention, positional encoding, encoder/decoder structure, and O(n²) efficiency improvements.

cxl-compute-express-link.title: CXL (Compute Express Link) High-Speed Interconnect
cxl-compute-express-link.summary: An open standard that layers cache coherence and memory semantics on the PCIe physical layer to connect CPUs, accelerators, and memory with low latency—covering the three layers CXL.io/cache/mem, Type 1/2/3 devices, and resolving the memory wall and idle waste in AI and data centers through memory expansion, pooling, and sharing.

risc-v.title: RISC-V (Open Instruction Set Architecture)
risc-v.summary: An open, royalty-free instruction set architecture originating at UC Berkeley. By layering standard and custom extensions modularly onto a small, fixed base integer ISA (RV32I/RV64I), it enables freedom from licensing lock-in and domain-specific computing, spreading from embedded systems to AI and servers.

platform-engineering.title: Platform Engineering
platform-engineering.summary: An approach that productizes infrastructure, tools, and standards into a self-service Internal Developer Platform (IDP) and provides golden paths to lower developers' cognitive load and improve software delivery speed and stability—understood as a product and means for realizing DevOps and SRE at organizational scale.

zero-knowledge-proof.title: Zero-Knowledge Proof (ZKP)
zero-knowledge-proof.summary: A cryptographic protocol that proves knowledge of a secret, or the truth of a statement, without revealing the secret. Satisfying completeness, soundness, and zero-knowledge, it is implemented in interactive/non-interactive (Fiat-Shamir) forms and via zk-SNARK and zk-STARK, emerging as the core of zk-Rollup blockchain scaling and privacy-preserving identity proof (selective disclosure).

ebpf.title: eBPF (extended Berkeley Packet Filter)
ebpf.summary: A programmable kernel technology that attaches verified sandboxed programs to kernel events—without recompiling or rebooting the kernel—to handle networking, observability, and security in a unified, high-performance way.

reinforcement-learning.title: Reinforcement Learning
reinforcement-learning.summary: A paradigm in which an agent learns an optimal policy that maximizes cumulative delayed, evaluative rewards through trial-and-error interaction with an environment—covering value-based, policy-based, and actor-critic families, the exploration-exploitation balance, and extension to LLM alignment via RLHF.

ai-agent.title: AI Agents and Agentic AI
ai-agent.summary: A system that combines an LLM 'brain' with planning, memory, tools, and actions to autonomously repeat observe-think-act loops until a goal is achieved—spreading around ReAct, multi-agent designs, and the MCP standard, where balancing autonomy against control and safety is key.

knowledge-graph.title: Knowledge Graph
knowledge-graph.summary: A knowledge base that represents entities as nodes and relationships as edges in triples, treating meaning and connections as first-class citizens—built around RDF and property-graph models, ontology reasoning, and graph embeddings for search, recommendation, and fraud detection, and re-emerging as an explainable knowledge source that curbs LLM hallucination via GraphRAG.

mitre-attack.title: MITRE ATT&CK (Cyber Attack Tactics and Techniques Knowledge Base)
mitre-attack.summary: An open knowledge base that systematizes attack behaviors observed in real-world breaches into tactics, techniques, and procedures (TTPs)—focusing on adversary behavior rather than IoCs and serving as a common language for detection-gap analysis, threat hunting, and adversary emulation.

decentralized-identity.title: Decentralized Identity (DID)
decentralized-identity.summary: A self-sovereign identity model that returns control of identity information from institutions to users—cryptographically verifying against forgery and tampering without excessive collection, through the issuer-holder-verifier trust triangle, VC/VP, and selective disclosure.

consistent-hashing.title: Consistent Hashing
consistent-hashing.summary: A distribution technique that places keys and nodes on a single hash ring and assigns each key to the first node clockwise, minimizing remapping to an average of K/N when nodes are added or removed—using virtual nodes to ensure load balance and weighting, and serving as the standard routing foundation for distributed stores, caches, and load balancers.

cdn.title: Content Delivery Network (CDN)
cdn.summary: Infrastructure that replicates content across geographically distributed edge-server caches and directs users to the optimal edge to reduce latency and distribute origin load—covering pull/push caching and invalidation strategies, DDoS and WAF security, and its evolution into a distributed delivery platform via edge computing.

mixture-of-experts.title: Mixture of Experts (MoE)
mixture-of-experts.summary: A large-scale AI scaling architecture in which a gating network selectively activates only a few experts per token—conditional computation that decouples total parameters (knowledge capacity) from active parameters (compute), realizing a far larger model within the same compute budget—covering routing, load balancing, expert parallelism, and comparison with dense models.

webassembly.title: WebAssembly (Wasm)
webassembly.summary: A portable binary instruction format that compiles from many languages to run safely at near-native speed in browsers, servers, and at the edge—a lightweight isolated execution layer based on a stack VM, linear memory, and capability-based isolation, extended by WASI and the component model.

chiplet.title: Chiplet Architecture and Heterogeneous Integration
chiplet.summary: An approach that, instead of one large monolithic die, heterogeneously integrates smaller dies divided by function and process node into a single package using the UCIe standard D2D interconnect and 2.5D/3D packaging—a semiconductor design and packaging architecture that overcomes the cost, yield, and reticle limits of advanced process nodes and forms the foundation for AI chips and HBM integration.

explainable-ai.title: Explainable AI (XAI)
explainable-ai.summary: A technology that presents the reasoning, contributing factors, and decision process of black-box models such as deep learning in human-understandable form (LIME, SHAP, Grad-CAM) to ensure transparency, trustworthiness, and accountability—balancing the accuracy–interpretability–cost trade-off on a purpose- and risk-based basis and forming a core pillar of AI trustworthiness and regulatory compliance such as the EU AI Act.

multimodal-ai.title: Multimodal AI
multimodal-ai.summary: A technology that aligns heterogeneous modalities—text, image, audio, and video—into a common semantic space (CLIP contrastive learning) and fuses them via early, late, and cross-attention to achieve complementary understanding and generation—where overcoming inter-modal heterogeneity and controlling hallucination and bias are the challenges; it is the standard form of foundation models and a key path toward VLA and embodied intelligence.

gitops.title: GitOps — A Git-Based Declarative Operations Model
gitops.summary: An operations model that declaratively stores the system's desired state in Git and has an in-cluster agent continuously reconcile the actual state (pull, self-healing)—achieving safe, reproducible deployments through curbing configuration drift, full auditability, minimal exposure of cluster credentials, and git-revert rollback, and forming the foundation of autonomous operations when combined with IaC, DevSecOps, and platform engineering.

data-fabric.title: Data Fabric
data-fabric.summary: A technology-centric data-management architecture that weaves discovery, integration, governance, and delivery into a single logical layer across distributed, heterogeneous data—without physically consolidating it—using active metadata, knowledge graphs, and AI automation. It minimizes data movement through data virtualization and automatically enforces lineage-based governance, becoming effective when combined complementarily with the organization-centric data mesh.

raid.title: RAID (Redundant Array of Independent Disks)
raid.summary: A storage technology that combines multiple disks through striping, mirroring, and parity to gain both performance and fault tolerance—covering the trade-offs of RAID 0/1/5/6/10 levels, the write penalty and rebuild risk, and recent trends such as distributed RAID and erasure coding, and noting that RAID is not a backup and must be paired with DR.

bloom-filter.title: Bloom Filter
bloom-filter.summary: A probabilistic data structure that determines set membership using only an m-bit array and k hash functions; 'not present' is 100% accurate while only 'present' allows false positives, cheaply filtering large-scale membership queries with minimal memory—covering its operating principle, the false-positive-probability sizing formula (m/n·ln2), use cases such as LSM databases and safe browsing, and trade-offs against counting and cuckoo filters.

webrtc.title: WebRTC (Web Real-Time Communication)
webrtc.summary: An open technology that transmits audio, video, and data peer-to-peer with ultra-low latency using only standard browser APIs (getUserMedia, RTCPeerConnection, RTCDataChannel) without plugins—covering SDP offer/answer signaling, ICE (STUN/TURN)-based NAT traversal, mandatory SRTP/DTLS encryption, the Mesh/SFU/MCU scaling structures, trade-offs against HLS/WebSocket, and infrastructure-sizing and security considerations.

togaf-ea.title: TOGAF and Enterprise Architecture (EA)
togaf-ea.summary: Covers the EA discipline, which draws an enterprise-wide blueprint across the business, data, application, and technology (BDAT) layers to align an organization's business strategy with IT and achieve deduplication, standardization, and interoperability, and TOGAF, the open standard that implements it through an iterative process (ADM), reference models, and governance. An essay-style overview including comparison with Zachman and FEAF, the eight ADM phases and requirements management, EA maturity, the reinterpretation of lightweight governance in the cloud and MSA era, and the importance of using EA for decision-making rather than as documentation.

knowledge-distillation.title: Knowledge Distillation
knowledge-distillation.summary: A leading model-compression technique that transfers the soft targets (tacit knowledge, inter-class similarity) of a large, high-performing teacher model to a small student model via temperature scaling and KL-divergence loss, reducing parameters, computation, and latency while preserving accuracy as much as possible. An essay-style overview of the soft-target principle, the combination of temperature and loss, the response/feature/relation/self-distillation types, comparison and combination with pruning and quantization, and Professional-Engineer-level considerations such as the teacher-student capacity gap, data licensing, and bias transfer.

sovereign-cloud.title: Sovereign Cloud
sovereign-cloud.summary: A cloud designed so that the storage, processing, operation, and control of data are self-contained within a specific country's laws and jurisdiction, guaranteeing data sovereignty across three layers—data, operations, and technology. An essay-style overview of why data residency alone is insufficient and must be combined with cryptographic-key sovereignty (HYOK/BYOK), access transparency, and open-standard portability; the background of jurisdictional conflicts such as the CLOUD Act and Schrems II; the three-layer sovereignty structure and reference architecture; a comparison of deployment types (domestic region, partner-operated, dedicated isolation, and domestically built standalone); and domestic and international trends and trade-offs such as GAIA-X and CSAP.

diffusion-model.title: Diffusion Model
diffusion-model.summary: A generative deep-learning model composed of a forward diffusion process that progressively adds noise to data and a reverse diffusion process that undoes it with a neural network (U-Net/DiT). An essay-style overview of the principle of decomposing generation into a multi-step denoising problem to secure both training stability and quality/diversity, DDPM's forward and reverse processes and noise/loss structure, the compute-saving principles of conditional generation (Classifier-Free Guidance) and latent diffusion (LDM/Stable Diffusion), a quality/diversity/speed trade-off comparison with GANs and VAEs, evaluation metrics such as FID, and governance considerations such as copyright, deepfakes, and watermarking.

siem.title: SIEM (Security Information and Event Management)
siem.summary: An integrated security-monitoring platform that collects, normalizes, and correlates heterogeneous logs and events from across the organization in real time to detect multi-stage threats and provide compliance evidence and a basis for incident investigation. An essay-style overview of the data pipeline from collection → normalization → storage → correlation → alerting and the principles of rule- and statistics-based (UEBA) detection, its relationship to and differences from log management, SOAR, and XDR, recent trends that overcome alert fatigue, cost, and detection-coverage limits through AI-SIEM, data lakes, cloud-native design, and XDR integration, and Professional-Engineer-level considerations such as collection-policy design, rule tuning, and combining analyst expertise.

processing-in-memory.title: Processing-in-Memory (PIM)
processing-in-memory.summary: A data-centric semiconductor architecture that integrates compute units inside memory (DRAM) to perform computation in place without moving data to the processor, mitigating the memory wall of the von Neumann architecture and the power cost of data movement. An essay-style overview of the operating principle exploiting bank-level parallelism, types by compute-unit placement (bank, logic die, PNM) and by circuit method (digital, analog crossbar), the offloading execution flow, per-memory application cases such as HBM-PIM, GDDR6-AiM, and CXL-PNM and comparison with GPUs and neuromorphic computing, and Professional-Engineer-level considerations such as selective-offloading strategy, area/heat/precision trade-offs, and the standards (JEDEC, CXL) ecosystem.

dlp.title: DLP (Data Loss Prevention)
dlp.summary: A data-centric security framework that identifies, monitors, and blocks sensitive and confidential data across its at-rest, in-motion, and in-use states using content inspection, preventing both intentional exfiltration and inadvertent exposure. This essay covers controls for the three data states (Network, Endpoint, and Storage DLP) and the overall architecture, detection techniques such as patterns, dictionaries, EDM/fingerprinting, and ML together with their combination and tuning, the operational flow of risk-based graduated responses (log, alert, encrypt, block), the relationship with adjacent technologies like DRM, CASB, and UEBA, the deployment process from classification and policy design through monitoring, enforcement, and continuous improvement, and professional-engineer considerations such as SASE/SSE extension for the cloud, remote-work, and generative-AI era and the trade-off between privacy and false positives.

xdr.title: XDR (eXtended Detection and Response)
xdr.summary: A threat-response framework that collects, normalizes, and correlates telemetry from endpoints, network, email, cloud, and identity on a single platform, automatically reconstructing scattered alerts into a single attack story (incident) and unifying and automating detection, investigation, and response as one flow. This essay covers the overall architecture spanning sensors, core (data lake, correlation engine, ML/UEBA), and response, the operational flow of detect, triage, investigate, contain, and recover, the principles of ATT&CK-chain-based incident reconstruction, a comparison of Native versus Open (Hybrid) XDR and its boundaries with SIEM, SOAR, and EDR, recent trends such as generative-AI copilots, SASE/SSE extension, MDR as-a-service consumption, and OCSF standardization, and professional-engineer considerations including data quality, false-positive tuning, vendor lock-in, privacy, Zero Trust integration, and organizational maturity.

cyber-kill-chain.title: Cyber Kill Chain
cyber-kill-chain.summary: A defense-oriented, intelligence-driven framework that decomposes targeted cyberattacks into a seven-stage chain of reconnaissance, weaponization, delivery, exploitation, installation, command and control (C2), and actions on objectives, neutralizing a breach even when only a single stage is blocked. This essay covers the adversary behavior and defensive controls at each stage, layered-defense design through the Courses of Action matrix (detect, deny, disrupt, degrade, deceive) and gap analysis of defensive coverage, a comparison with MITRE ATT&CK, the Diamond Model, and the Unified Kill Chain along with strategies for combining them, structural limitations such as perimeter bias and linear assumptions and its evolution to address cloud and insider threats, integration with SIEM, SOAR, and XDR and its application to threat hunting, and professional-engineer considerations such as Zero Trust, blocking to the left, and campaign intelligence.

edge-computing.title: Edge Computing
edge-computing.summary: A distributed computing paradigm that performs computation, storage, and analysis on distributed resources near where data is generated, resolving latency, bandwidth, and privacy problems. This essay covers the layered structure spanning device, edge (on-device, near, far), and cloud and the principle of data gravity, ETSI MEC and 5G local breakout architectures, task-offloading decisions and orchestration based on lightweight Kubernetes (K3s, KubeEdge), hierarchical aggregation and disconnection-tolerant, resilient design, a comparison of latency, cost, and consistency trade-offs with the central cloud, application cases in smart factories, autonomous driving, immersive media, and smart cities, recent trends such as edge AI, federated learning, 6G, edge serverless, and confidential computing, and professional-engineer considerations including selective workload placement, security, operational complexity, and adoption roadmap.

deadlock.title: Deadlock
deadlock.summary: This essay covers the definition of deadlock and its distinction from starvation and livelock, the four necessary conditions (mutual exclusion, hold and wait, no preemption, and circular wait), detection via resource-allocation graphs, the trade-offs among prevention, avoidance (banker's algorithm), detection, and recovery techniques, practical cases in databases, multithreading, and distributed systems along with the dining-philosophers problem, and professional-engineer considerations such as lock ordering, timeouts, retries, and observability.

waf.title: WAF (Web Application Firewall)
waf.summary: This essay covers the definition of a WAF and the background behind application-layer (L7) defense, the overall structure spanning normalization, detection, and decision along with deployment modes such as reverse proxy, transparent bridge, out-of-band, and cloud-based, the trade-offs among negative (signatures, OWASP CRS), positive (whitelist), and anomaly/bot-management detection models, defense against OWASP Top 10 threats such as SQLi and XSS along with the Log4Shell virtual-patching case, a comparison with IPS, RASP, and API gateways, evolution toward WAAP and cloud WAF, and professional-engineer considerations such as false-positive tuning, SSL decryption, SPOF, and regulatory compliance.

data-contract.title: Data Contracts and Data Product Reliability
data-contract.summary: A data-product interface in which data producers and consumers explicitly agree on the meaning, schema, quality, freshness, access, and service level of data and automatically validate them. Going beyond the limits of fixing only the schema, this essay covers the components of a contract, its lifecycle, compatibility and versioning strategies, dbt model contracts and ODCS integration, and operational considerations in data-mesh and DataOps environments.

slsa-software-supply-chain.title: SLSA-Based Software Supply Chain Security and Build Integrity
slsa-software-supply-chain.summary: This essay explains how to verify the integrity of the path by which software flows from source to distributed artifacts, centering on SLSA's Build and Source tracks and provenance. It describes the difference from an SBOM, attack scenarios, CI/CD implementation, and verification, policy, and operational considerations in a professional-engineer essay format.

data-warehouse-olap.title: Data Warehouse and OLAP
data-warehouse-olap.summary: This essay covers the structure of a data warehouse, an analytics-only store separated from operational systems (OLTP) that accumulates history under the principles of subject orientation, integration, time-variance, and non-volatility, along with ETL/ELT pipelines, dimensional modeling (star, snowflake, SCD), OLAP operations and a comparison of MOLAP/ROLAP/HOLAP, and its evolution toward the cloud DW and the lakehouse, in a professional-engineer essay format.

rpo-rto-disaster-recovery.title: Disaster Recovery Strategy Based on RPO, RTO, and MTTR
rpo-rto-disaster-recovery.summary: This essay covers a disaster recovery strategy that defines RPO, RTO, MTTR, and MTD based on business impact analysis (BIA) and combines backup, replication, multi-region deployment, and recovery drills to control service disruption and data loss.

ipv6.title: IPv6 and IPv4-to-IPv6 Transition Technologies
ipv6.summary: This essay covers IPv6, the next-generation Internet protocol that resolves IPv4 exhaustion and the limits of scalability and security through 128-bit addressing, a fixed header, SLAAC/NDP, and integrated IPsec, and addresses IPv4-to-IPv6 transition technologies such as dual stack, tunneling, and NAT64 along with IPv6-specific security threats such as RA spoofing and their countermeasures from an in-depth perspective.

site-reliability-engineering.title: SRE (Site Reliability Engineering) and Service Reliability Management
site-reliability-engineering.summary: An engineering discipline that designs software from an operations perspective and, through SLIs, SLOs, error budgets, and incident response, manages the balance between service reliability and development velocity.

secure-coding.title: Secure Coding and Software Development Security
secure-coding.summary: Development-security activities that integrate security across all SDLC phases to proactively eliminate vulnerabilities at the design and implementation stages — an in-depth treatment covering secure-coding rules such as input validation and output encoding, the seven vulnerability categories, embedding threat modeling and SAST/DAST/IAST/SCA analysis into CI/CD, and extension to AI, supply chain, and DevSecOps.

architecture-tradeoff-analysis-method.title: Software Architecture Evaluation Based on ATAM (Architecture Tradeoff Analysis Method)
architecture-tradeoff-analysis-method.summary: This essay covers the ATAM evaluation method, which identifies architectural risks, sensitivity points, and trade-offs based on business drivers and quality-attribute scenarios and links them to stakeholder consensus and decision records, in a professional-engineer essay format.

bulkhead-pattern.title: The Bulkhead Pattern and Fault Isolation
bulkhead-pattern.summary: The principle, implementation levels, and operational strategy of the bulkhead pattern, which partitions shared resources into independent pools so that the latency or exhaustion of one dependency does not propagate to other functions.

model-context-protocol.title: MCP (Model Context Protocol)
model-context-protocol.summary: The structure, primitives, transport, and security threats of MCP — an open protocol that connects LLM applications with external tools, data, and prompts in a standardized way through a Host-Client-Server structure and JSON-RPC 2.0, reducing the M×N integration problem to M+N — along with professional-engineer implications.

opentelemetry-observability.title: Distributed Tracing and Unified Observability with OpenTelemetry
opentelemetry-observability.summary: How to collect and correlate traces, metrics, and logs with OpenTelemetry, the vendor-neutral instrumentation standard, and design observability for distributed systems using the Collector, OTLP, and semantic conventions.

htap.title: HTAP (Hybrid Transactional/Analytical Processing)
htap.summary: An architecture that processes OLTP and OLAP in a single engine without ETL through in-memory and row/column hybrid storage and workload isolation, providing real-time analytics on operational data — its implementation types, core technologies, and trade-offs.

feature-store.title: Feature Store and Machine Learning Data Operations
feature-store.summary: This essay covers the components of a feature store that centralizes the definition, transformation, validation, and lineage of machine-learning features and serves them consistently to offline training and online inference, along with point-in-time correctness and data-leakage prevention, batch and streaming operations, and quality, security, and governance strategies, in a professional-engineer essay format.

pki.title: PKI (Public Key Infrastructure)
pki.summary: This essay covers the components and certificate lifecycle of PKI, which binds a public key to an identity in an X.509 certificate via a CA's digital signature and makes it verifiable through a hierarchical chain of trust, revocation (CRL/OCSP), and repositories, along with a comparison of trust models, trends such as ACME automation, CT transparency, and the post-quantum (PQC) transition, and professional-engineer considerations.

graphrag.title: GraphRAG (Graph Retrieval-Augmented Generation)
graphrag.summary: The structure, retrieval methods, construction process, and evaluation and operational strategy of GraphRAG, which extracts entities, relationships, and communities from unstructured documents and combines hierarchical summarization with graph traversal to overcome the local-retrieval limits of ordinary RAG.

quantum-safe-cryptography.title: Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC) and Cryptographic Transition Strategy
