quantum-safe-cryptography.summary: A strategy that counters Shor and HNDL threats by using ML-KEM, ML-DSA, and SLH-DSA and transitions PKI and the supply chain in stages through a cryptographic-asset inventory, risk prioritization, hybrid piloting, and crypto agility.

bgp.title: BGP (Border Gateway Protocol)
bgp.summary: The backbone Internet protocol that exchanges policy-based reachability between ASes using AS_PATH and path attributes (LOCAL_PREF, MED, Community) — eBGP/iBGP, best-path selection, a comparison with IGPs, and RPKI-based security.

iso-42001-ai-management-system.title: ISO/IEC 42001:2023 Artificial Intelligence Management System (AIMS)
iso-42001-ai-management-system.summary: This essay covers the requirements of an AI management system (AIMS) for developing, providing, and using AI responsibly, along with risk and impact assessment, lifecycle controls, and an implementation roadmap.

message-queue-kafka.title: Message Queues and Apache Kafka
message-queue-kafka.summary: This essay provides an in-depth treatment of the communication model of message queues, which decouple producers and consumers via a buffer to achieve asynchronous, loose coupling, and of the architecture, delivery semantics, and trade-offs of Apache Kafka, which supports durable storage, reprocessing, and horizontal scaling of high-volume events based on a distributed commit log.

technical-debt.title: Technical Debt Management and Repayment Strategy
technical-debt.summary: The causes, types, measurement, and management lifecycle of technical debt — incurred by accepting future change and operational costs for the sake of fast delivery — and a sustainable repayment strategy.

time-series-database.title: Time Series Database
time-series-database.summary: This essay provides an in-depth treatment of the data model of a time series database that treats time as a first-class axis and optimizes append-only high-volume ingestion, time-axis compression (delta/Gorilla), range aggregation, downsampling, and retention policies, along with its LSM-based storage engine, a comparison of product types, and practical application to observability and IoT.

data-lineage-impact-analysis.title: Data Lineage and Impact Analysis
data-lineage-impact-analysis.summary: This essay covers a data governance framework that traces the path by which data flows from source to transformation, storage, analysis, and service as a Dataset-Job-Run graph and analyzes change impact, root cause of failures, and personal-data propagation.

api-management.title: API Management and API Lifecycle Governance
api-management.summary: A governance framework that manages APIs as a single lifecycle spanning contract, portal, gateway, security, observability, change, and retirement, improving reusability, stability, and consumer experience.

sd-wan.title: SD-WAN (Software-Defined WAN)
sd-wan.summary: A WAN architecture that applies SDN's plane-separation principle to the wide-area network, binding Internet, LTE, and MPLS circuits with an encrypted overlay and centrally controlling paths in software according to application-aware policies and real-time link quality.

ai-sbom.title: AI Software BOM (AI SBOM) and Artificial Intelligence Supply Chain Transparency
ai-sbom.summary: This essay covers, in a professional-engineer answer format, the concept, standards, and collection, verification, and operational strategy of an AI Software BOM that manages the composition and relationships of models, data, code, pipelines, infrastructure, and external services in a machine-readable form.

npu.title: NPU (Neural Processing Unit)
npu.summary: This essay covers, in a professional-engineer answer format, the architecture, dataflow, performance metrics, comparison with CPUs and GPUs, and recent trends of the NPU, an AI-dedicated accelerator that specializes and accelerates the multiply-accumulate operations of neural networks through systolic arrays, low-precision arithmetic, and data reuse.

llmops.title: LLMOps (Large Language Model Operations) and Generative-AI Service Lifecycle Management
llmops.summary: This essay covers, in a professional-engineer answer format, the management of prompts, models, retrieval augmentation, tools, evaluation, observability, security, and cost, along with a continuous-improvement framework, for taking large-language-model-based applications from experimentation to production.

ctem.title: CTEM (Continuous Threat Exposure Management)
ctem.summary: This essay covers, in an answer format, the five-stage cycle of CTEM, which continuously discovers, prioritizes, validates, and remediates exposure spanning assets, misconfigurations, privileges, and attack surface from the attacker's perspective, along with its reference architecture, its differences from traditional vulnerability management and penetration testing, an adoption roadmap, and professional-engineer considerations.

rpa-intelligent-automation.title: RPA (Robotic Process Automation) and Intelligent Process Automation (IPA)
rpa-intelligent-automation.summary: This essay addresses how to extend RPA — which automates repetitive tasks with rule-based software robots — into intelligent process automation by combining it with process mining, IDP, and AI. It covers target selection, architecture, operational governance, security, and performance measurement in an essay format.

microservices-architecture.title: Microservices Architecture (MSA)
microservices-architecture.summary: This essay covers, in an essay format, service decomposition along domain boundaries, API and event-based communication, distributed data consistency, fault isolation, and incremental migration strategy.

threat-modeling.title: Threat Modeling
threat-modeling.summary: This essay covers, in an essay format, a Shift-Left security activity that structures the system with a DFD, exhaustively derives threats with STRIDE, prioritizes them with DREAD and CVSS, and proactively mitigates risk at the design stage.

fuzz-testing.title: Fuzz Testing and Vulnerability Detection Strategy
fuzz-testing.summary: This essay covers the principles and application strategy of fuzz testing, which automatically generates and mutates abnormal and boundary inputs to find crashes, memory errors, state-transition violations, and business-rule defects.

load-balancing.title: Load Balancing and L4/L7 Traffic Distribution
load-balancing.summary: A technique that distributes requests across multiple servers to secure availability, scalability, and performance — this essay covers the difference between high-speed IP/port-based L4 and fine-grained content-based L7, distribution algorithms, health checks, session externalization, GSLB, and redundancy, and its evolution toward the cloud and the service mesh.

differential-privacy.title: Differential Privacy and the Privacy Budget
differential-privacy.summary: This essay covers the definition of differential privacy, which bounds the difference in output probability between adjacent datasets by ε and δ, along with sensitivity and the Laplace and Gaussian mechanisms, composition and privacy accounting, a comparison with de-identification, federated learning, and homomorphic encryption, and application strategies for public statistics, service analytics, and DP training.

ci-cd-pipeline.title: CI/CD Pipeline (Continuous Integration / Continuous Deployment)
ci-cd-pipeline.summary: This essay covers the structure and principles of a CI/CD pipeline that implements the software-delivery process from commit to deployment as an automation chain of build, test, quality gate, and deployment — the difference between CI (small, frequent integration with immediate verification) and continuous delivery/deployment, zero-downtime deployment strategies, quality gates, DevSecOps, and supply chain security, environment-promotion principles, and DORA-metrics-based management along with a professional-engineer application strategy.

data-observability.title: Data Observability and Data Reliability Management
data-observability.summary: A data-reliability operations framework that collects freshness, completeness, validity, distribution, and lineage signals to detect data anomalies and connects them to impact analysis, recovery, and post-incident improvement.

ebpf-kernel-observability.title: eBPF-Based Kernel Visibility, Security, and Networking
ebpf-kernel-observability.summary: This essay covers the execution model of eBPF, which attaches verifier- and JIT-processed kernel programs to hooks to dynamically extend networking, tracing, and security functions, along with maps, BTF, and CO-RE, its use in XDP, observability, and security, a comparison with traditional approaches, and a safe adoption and operations strategy.

cmmi.title: CMMI (Capability Maturity Model Integration)
cmmi.summary: A performance-oriented framework that diagnoses and improves an organization's process capability across five maturity levels (Initial, Managed, Defined, Quantitatively Managed, Optimizing) and four capability levels. This essay covers the representations (continuous and staged), practice areas and domains, the appraisal (Benchmark, Sustainment, Evaluation) procedures, a comparison with SPICE and ISO 9001, integration with Agile and DevOps, and the V3.0 (2023, ISACA) extension.

cloud-native.title: Cloud Native Architecture
cloud-native.summary: This essay covers the principles, layered structure, security and operations, comparison cases, and phased-migration strategy of cloud native, which combines containers, microservices, declarative APIs, automation, observability, and elasticity to respond repeatably to change and failure.

btree-bplus-index.title: Database Index Structures (B-Tree and B+Tree)
btree-bplus-index.summary: This essay covers the B-Tree, a balanced multi-way search tree that increases fan-out by mapping a node to a disk page, and the B+Tree, which places data only in leaves and links them as a linked list to strengthen range and sort queries — their structures, operations (search, split, merge), and comparison, along with clustered/covering indexes and anti-patterns, and the changes brought by the LSM-Tree and SSD era.

itil-4.title: ITIL 4 (IT Infrastructure Library) and Service Management
itil-4.summary: An in-depth note on ITIL 4, designing the operation and improvement framework for digital services through the Service Value System (SVS), the four dimensions, the seven guiding principles, the value chain, and management practices.

mqtt.title: MQTT (Message Queuing Telemetry Transport)
mqtt.summary: A publish/subscribe-based lightweight IoT messaging protocol — an in-depth note covering brokers, topics, QoS 0/1/2, LWT, Retain, and Keep Alive, through to MQTT 5.0 (shared subscriptions, User Property).

database-replication-high-availability.title: Database Replication and High-Availability Design
database-replication-high-availability.summary: Organizes database high-availability design and operational strategy around synchronous/asynchronous replication, single- and multi-leader topologies, replication lag and read consistency, failover, fencing, RPO, and RTO.

llm-as-a-judge.title: LLM-as-a-Judge (LLM-Based Evaluation)
llm-as-a-judge.summary: A method for using an LLM as an evaluator to measure accuracy, relevance, groundedness, and safety with rubrics — covering deterministic metrics, human meta-evaluation, bias control, RAG and agent evaluation, and operational deployment gates.

dns.title: DNS (Domain Name System) and DNS Security
dns.summary: A hierarchical, distributed name-resolution system that translates domain names into IP addresses — covering recursive/iterative queries and caching principles, record types, threats such as cache poisoning and amplification DDoS, and mitigations including DNSSEC (integrity) and DoH/DoT (confidentiality).

mvcc-snapshot-concurrency-control.title: MVCC (Multi-Version Concurrency Control) and Snapshot-Based Transactions
mvcc-snapshot-concurrency-control.summary: Organizes MVCC, which reduces read/write contention via per-transaction snapshots and multiple row versions — covering visibility determination, isolation levels, PostgreSQL/InnoDB implementations, version cleanup, locking, serialization retries, and operational design.

solid-principles.title: SOLID Object-Oriented Design Principles
solid-principles.summary: Object-oriented design principles that separate responsibilities via the five principles SRP, OCP, LSP, ISP, and DIP and control dependency direction and size through abstraction to achieve change-resilient design — a common language for maintainability that extends to Clean Architecture and MSA.

data-vault-modeling.title: Data Warehouse Modeling Based on Data Vault 2.0
data-vault-modeling.summary: A data warehouse modeling methodology that separates business keys, relationships, and attribute history into Hubs, Links, and Satellites and layers a Raw Vault and Business Vault to secure change resilience, auditability, and parallel loading. It also covers differences from star schema, 3NF, and the lakehouse, along with key, point-in-time, idempotency, quality, and privacy design.

gan.title: Generative Adversarial Network (GAN)
gan.summary: A generative model that approximates the real distribution by pitting a generator that creates data against a discriminator that judges authenticity in a minimax game. Provides an in-depth treatment of adversarial learning principles, DCGAN/cGAN/CycleGAN/StyleGAN variants, FID/IS evaluation metrics, comparison with diffusion models, handling of mode collapse and training instability, and trust/governance issues such as deepfakes.

ztna.title: ZTNA (Zero Trust Network Access)
ztna.summary: Organizes ZTNA, which distrusts network location and verifies user, device, context, and resource on a per-request basis to provide least-privilege, per-application access — covering its principles, PDP/PEP composition, comparison with VPN and SASE, adoption steps, and cloud-native extension.

data-catalog-metadata.title: Data Catalog and Metadata Management
data-catalog-metadata.summary: Organizes the concept and structure of a data catalog that links technical, business, operational, and governance metadata to data assets, glossaries, quality, lineage, and policy — covering collection, curation, search, and impact-analysis processes, ISO/IEC 11179 and W3C DCAT alignment, use in data products and AI, and adoption strategy.

common-criteria.title: Common Criteria (CC / ISO/IEC 15408)
common-criteria.summary: An international standard by which a third party evaluates and certifies the security functions (SFR) and assurance level (SAR/EAL) of security products through a standardized procedure — covering the PP/ST/TOE concepts, the evaluation/certification process, and trends including CCRA mutual recognition, cPP, and CC:2022.

hexagonal-architecture.title: Hexagonal Architecture (Ports and Adapters)
hexagonal-architecture.summary: A Ports and Adapters structure that abstracts the business core into ports and isolates REST, DB, messaging, and external APIs as adapters — covering driving/driven ports, dependency inversion, testing and operational strategy, and comparison with layered and Clean Architecture.

two-phase-commit.title: Two-Phase Commit (2PC) and Three-Phase Commit (3PC) Protocols
two-phase-commit.summary: 2PC (prepare/commit), which guarantees the atomicity of distributed transactions, and 3PC (pre-commit), which mitigates its blocking — covering coordinator/participant structure, log-based recovery, blocking and partition vulnerabilities, and comparison with XA, saga, and Paxos Commit alternatives.

transactional-outbox-pattern.title: Transactional Outbox Pattern
transactional-outbox-pattern.summary: A pattern that binds the dual-write problem of business data changes and event publishing into a single local transaction and delivers to the broker via an outbox and message relay — organizing polling publisher and CDC approaches, duplication/ordering/reprocessing/retention policies, comparison with 2PC/saga/event sourcing, and adoption strategy.

lsm-tree.title: LSM Tree (Log-Structured Merge-Tree)
lsm-tree.summary: A write-optimized storage structure that gathers random writes in a MemTable, flushes them sequentially, and organizes immutable SSTables via background compaction — organizing WAL, Bloom filter, tombstone, and MVCC behavior, leveled/size-tiered compaction and the read/write/space amplification (RUM) trade-off, comparison with B+ trees, and RocksDB/Cassandra application cases.

distributed-lock.title: Distributed Lock
distributed-lock.summary: The structure and protocols of a distributed lock that implements mutual exclusion via atomic acquisition, leasing, owner tokens, and fencing tokens so that multiple servers do not modify a shared resource simultaneously. It compares database, Redis, and consensus-based coordinators, and covers TTL expiration and zombie-client handling, conditional updates, idempotency, and operational strategy.

digital-twin.title: Digital Twin Architecture and Implementation Strategy
digital-twin.summary: The concept and reference architecture of a digital twin that synchronizes an observable real-world target with its digital representation for observation, prediction, simulation, and optimization. Covers the physical, edge, integration, twin-core, model, and application layers, data contracts, real-time behavior, interoperability and security, manufacturing/building/supply-chain cases, and an ISO 23247-based composition strategy.

rate-limiting.title: Rate Limiting and Traffic-Control Algorithms
rate-limiting.summary: A traffic-control technique that caps the number of requests within a time window — covering token bucket, leaky bucket, and fixed/sliding window algorithms, gateway- and Redis-based distributed implementations, and use of 429 and Retry-After responses to secure availability, fairness, cost, and security.

data-product.title: Data Product Design and Operation
data-product.summary: The design and operational strategy of a data product that bundles data, metadata, code, infrastructure, and operational accountability into a single product delivering independent value for analytics, AI, and business decisions — covering data mesh domain ownership; discoverability, addressability, understandability, interoperability, and security; and the lifecycle from quality contracts, SLAs, and versioning to retirement, plus organizational adoption.

owasp-top-10.title: OWASP Top 10 (Web Application Security Risks)
owasp-top-10.summary: The awareness standard for the top 10 web application security risks, selected from real vulnerability data (CVE) and expert surveys — providing an in-depth treatment of the 2025 revision's per-item principles (A01 Access Control through A10 Improper Exception Handling), changes from 2021 (rise of supply-chain failures and misconfiguration, SSRF consolidation), Shift-Left embedding in the SDLC/DevSecOps, and alignment with ASVS, SAMM, and the API/LLM Top 10.

owasp-api-security-top-10.title: API Security Design and Operation Based on OWASP API Security Top 10 (2023)
owasp-api-security-top-10.summary: Analyzes the top 10 risks of OWASP API Security Top 10 (2023) from the perspectives of object-, property-, and function-level authorization and resource and business-flow control, and organizes design/operational responses at the gateway, service, and data layers.

lambda-kappa-architecture.title: Lambda Architecture and Kappa Architecture
lambda-kappa-architecture.summary: Compares Lambda, which merges accuracy and real-time behavior through its three batch, speed, and serving layers, with Kappa, which unifies real-time processing and reprocessing through a single stream of an immutable log, and organizes consistency principles, reprocessing strategy, and lakehouse integration.

kubernetes-operator-pattern.title: Kubernetes Operator Pattern
kubernetes-operator-pattern.summary: Organizes the structure, implementation, and operational strategy of the operator pattern, which extends the Kubernetes API with CRDs and controllers to automate application domain knowledge through declarative management and reconciliation loops.

dora-metrics.title: DORA Software Delivery Performance Metrics (DORA Metrics)
dora-metrics.summary: Organizes how to measure and improve both software delivery throughput and instability together through change lead time, deployment frequency, time to restore from a failed deployment, change failure rate, and rework rate.

cnapp.title: CNAPP (Cloud-Native Application Protection Platform)
cnapp.summary: A cloud-native integrated security platform that consolidates and correlates fragmented cloud security functions such as CSPM, CWPP, CIEM, KSPM, and DSPM, and prioritizes risk around genuinely exploitable attack paths from code to runtime.

c4-adr-architecture-documentation.title: Software Architecture Documentation Based on the C4 Model and ADRs
c4-adr-architecture-documentation.summary: An integrated documentation strategy that represents structure for each audience through C4's Context, Container, Component, and Code layers, and records the context, alternatives, and trade-offs of architectural decisions with ADRs.

crdt.title: CRDT (Conflict-Free Replicated Data Type)
crdt.summary: A replicated data type that, thanks to the commutativity, associativity, and idempotency of its merge operation, necessarily converges (SEC) to the same state even when multiple replicas update independently without coordination — covering state/operation-based types, G/PN-Counter, OR-Set, and sequence CRDT variants, comparison with consensus and OT, and application strategy for real-time collaboration and multi-region.

bitmap-index.title: Bitmap Index and Analytical Database Optimization
bitmap-index.summary: An index structure that, in low-cardinality, read-centric environments, represents the row set per value as a bit string and accelerates multi-condition analytical queries with AND/OR operations, along with comparison with B-Tree and hash, bitmap joins, DML trade-offs, and data warehouse application strategy.

kerberos.title: Kerberos Authentication Protocol
kerberos.summary: An intranet authentication protocol that achieves mutual authentication and SSO without exposing passwords via a KDC (AS/TGS), symmetric keys, tickets (TGT), and timestamps — covering the 3-phase, 6-message procedure, cross-realm and delegation, Golden/Silver Ticket and Kerberoasting attacks and defenses, and hybrid SSO integration.

smart-contract-security.title: Smart Contract Security and Audit Strategy
smart-contract-security.summary: Based on the deterministic execution, asset custody, immutability, and gas constraints of smart contracts, models trust boundaries from the wallet through oracles and bridges, and organizes the causes and countermeasures for reentrancy, authorization, oracle, arithmetic, signature, and upgrade vulnerabilities, along with the test/audit/deploy/monitor lifecycle.

merkle-tree.title: Merkle Tree and Data Integrity Verification
merkle-tree.summary: A structure that hierarchically hashes data blocks, summarizes them into a single root hash, and verifies inclusion and integrity with an O(log n) Merkle path without transmitting the entire original — covering the construction and verification of a binary Merkle tree, odd-node handling, protocol-specific variants, application in blockchain, Git, and Certificate Transparency, and operational considerations.

critical-chain-project-management.title: Critical Chain Project Management (CCPM)
critical-chain-project-management.summary: A methodology that applies the Theory of Constraints (TOC) to schedule management to identify a critical chain accounting for both task and resource constraints, and aggregates and manages individual safety margins into project, feeding, and resource buffers (fever chart) to reduce losses from student syndrome, Parkinson's law, and multitasking, achieving on-time delivery and shorter lead times.

event-storming.title: Domain Exploration and Design Based on EventStorming
event-storming.summary: A workshop in which domain experts and developers jointly explore the terminology, rules, exceptions, responsibilities, and boundaries of complex business by laying domain events along a timeline — covering the Big Picture, Process, and Software Design stages, DDD/EDA/CQRS integration, hotspot management, and legacy modernization and facilitation strategy.

numa.title: Non-Uniform Memory Access (NUMA)
numa.summary: A ccNUMA structure that directly attaches local memory to each processor for scalability at the cost of differing local/remote access latency — providing an in-depth treatment of the composition of nodes, interconnects, and integrated memory controllers; locality alignment across the OS, application, and virtualization (vNUMA) layers such as first-touch, affinity, and interleave; false sharing and cache-coherence traffic; comparison with UMA and distributed memory; and extension to CXL and tiered memory.

bpmn-process-modeling.title: Business Process Modeling and Execution Based on BPMN 2.0
bpmn-process-modeling.summary: Organizes how to connect business processes from As-Is to To-Be and workflow automation, centered on BPMN's pools, lanes, events, activities, gateways, and message flows and their execution semantics, along with comparison with UML, flowcharts, and EventStorming, and exception, operational, and governance strategy.

write-ahead-logging.title: Write-Ahead Logging (WAL) and Database Recovery (ARIES)
write-ahead-logging.summary: Explains the WAL protocol of 'log before data' that guarantees atomicity and durability, along with log structure (LSN, physical/logical logging), checkpoints, and the three ARIES phases of analysis, redo, and undo with DPT, CLR, and repeating history via LSN-based scenarios, and organizes the steal/no-force policy trade-off and extension to replication, CDC, and cloud DBs.

eap-tls.title: Network Access Authentication Based on EAP-TLS (Extensible Authentication Protocol-Transport Layer Security)
eap-tls.summary: The principles, procedure, comparison, and operational strategy of a method that mutually authenticates the client and authentication server with X.509 certificates and the TLS handshake, and controls network access by combining 802.1X/RADIUS policy with the PKI lifecycle.

database-connection-pooling.title: Database Connection Pool Design and Tuning
database-connection-pooling.summary: Organizes the principles of a connection pool that reuses database connections to control connection-establishment cost and concurrency surges — covering lease/return/validation/timeout, pool sizing, comparison of application pools and external poolers, and failover, observability, and security design.

apache-iceberg.title: Open Table Format (Apache Iceberg)
apache-iceberg.summary: An in-depth treatment of Apache Iceberg, an engine-neutral open table format that gives snapshot-based ACID, hidden partitioning, schema/partition evolution, and time travel to a collection of files on object storage — covering its metadata-layer structure, operating principles, CoW/MoR and compaction, comparison with Delta/Hudi/Hive, and standardization trends.

policy-as-code.title: Policy as Code and Executable Governance
policy-as-code.summary: An executable-governance approach that version-controls security, compliance, and operational rules as declarative code and enforces them repeatedly across CI/CD, IaC, APIs, and Kubernetes runtime via PDP/PEP.

secrets-management.title: Secrets Management
secrets-management.summary: A system that separates credentials such as passwords, API keys, certificates, and encryption keys from code and centrally stores, issues, rotates, revokes, and audits them, shifting static secrets to dynamic, short-lived secrets and infrastructure-identity-based authentication to minimize the blast radius upon leakage.

data-centric-ai.title: Data-Centric AI and Training-Data Quality Engineering
data-centric-ai.summary: Organizes the concept, quality metrics, lifecycle, governance, and application strategy of DCAI, which systematically improves the quality, representativeness, labels, and lineage of data rather than model architecture to raise AI performance and reliability.

convolutional-neural-network.title: Convolutional Neural Network (CNN)
convolutional-neural-network.summary: A neural network that hierarchically extracts local features of an image via convolution and pooling — a standard image-recognition architecture that reduces parameters through local receptive fields and weight sharing and secures translation invariance.

digital-thread.title: Full-Lifecycle Information Linkage Based on the Digital Thread
digital-thread.summary: An essay-style treatment of the digital thread, which links requirements, design, manufacturing, inspection, operation, and maintenance data through common identifiers, standard semantics, versions, and lineage — covering its concept, reference architecture, impact analysis, standardization, quality/security/governance, and application to manufacturing and digital twins.

backend-for-frontend.title: BFF (Backend for Frontend) Pattern and Browser OAuth Security
backend-for-frontend.summary: Organizes the BFF pattern, which places a dedicated backend per client experience to compose, transform, and protect APIs, along with its architecture, organizational ownership, comparison with API gateways and GraphQL, and failure/performance/operational trade-offs, and connects it to the browser OAuth security recommendations of RFC 10017.

prompt-engineering.title: Prompt Engineering
prompt-engineering.summary: A low-cost technique that controls LLM output by designing the input (role, context, examples, format) without retraining the model — key techniques such as Zero/Few-shot, CoT, and ReAct, a comparison with RAG and fine-tuning, and prompt injection security and operational governance.

retrieval-augmented-generation.title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG)
retrieval-augmented-generation.summary: An essay-style overview of RAG, which retrieves external documents and data at query time and injects them into LLM generation — its reference architecture, ingestion, chunking, embedding, hybrid search, re-ranking, and citation verification, a comparison of basic, advanced, and agentic types, and evaluation, freshness, access control, prompt injection countermeasures, and adoption strategy.

privileged-access-management.title: Privileged Access Management (PAM)
privileged-access-management.summary: An essay-style overview of PAM, a security control framework that identifies, vaults, least-privileges, monitors, and revokes privileged accounts and sessions — account types (human, non-human, emergency), vaulting, password rotation, session management (PSM), PEDM, JIT/ZSP, and audit (UEBA) functions and architecture, a comparison with IAM and IGA, and cloud/DevOps extension and adoption strategy.

white-box-cryptography.title: White-box Cryptography
white-box-cryptography.summary: An essay-style overview of a software key-protection technique that fuses and hides keys within the algorithm using lookup tables and encoding, even under a white-box model where the attacker fully controls the execution environment — black/grey/white-box attack models, the implementation principles of key fusion, encoding, and masking, DRM and HCE payment applications, DCA and DFA attacks, and the trade-offs versus a TEE and layered defense.

digital-sovereignty.title: Digital Sovereignty and Cloud/AI Sovereignty
digital-sovereignty.summary: The ability to control legal jurisdiction, encryption keys, AI, technology, operations, and the supply chain beyond mere data storage location, and to switch independently when needed — business-risk-based assessment, a cloud sovereignty framework, and adoption and exit strategy.

privacy-de-identification.title: Personal Data De-identification and Privacy Protection Models (k-anonymity, l-diversity, t-closeness)
privacy-de-identification.summary: A privacy protection model and lifecycle governance that de-identifies identifiers, quasi-identifiers, and sensitive information through pseudonymization and generalization, then quantitatively verifies re-identification risk using k-anonymity (group size), l-diversity (value variety), and t-closeness (value distribution).

property-based-testing.title: Property-Based Testing and Generative Quality Verification
property-based-testing.summary: A generative quality-verification strategy that explores a broad input space using executable properties and domain generators, and links the shrunk minimal counterexample to regression tests.

ai-agent-orchestration.title: AI Agent Orchestration and Autonomous Task Execution Governance
ai-agent-orchestration.summary: An orchestration structure that coordinates goal decomposition, agent selection, tool execution, state management, and verification, and the design of authorization, approval, audit, and safety governance for autonomous execution.

feature-flag.title: Feature Flags and Progressive Delivery
feature-flag.summary: The types, lifecycle, and evaluation architecture of feature flags, which separate deployment from release and control feature exposure at runtime, along with strategies for progressive delivery, kill switches, and flag-debt management.

ai-red-teaming.title: Generative AI Red Teaming and Adversarial Security Testing
ai-red-teaming.summary: A continuous security-testing strategy that verifies generative AI models and applications from an attacker's perspective and links vulnerabilities in the model, implementation, infrastructure, and operational behavior to risk management and remediation.

green-software.title: Green Software and Sustainable Software Engineering
green-software.summary: Sustainable software engineering that reduces carbon emissions across the software lifecycle through the three principles of energy efficiency, carbon awareness, and hardware efficiency, measures emissions per functional unit with ISO/IEC 21031 (SCI), and links to ESG, FinOps, and Observability.

data-poisoning.title: AI Training-Data Poisoning Attacks and Data Integrity Defense
data-poisoning.summary: An overview of the types and threat models of poisoning attacks that insert or tamper with malicious content in training, fine-tuning, embedding, and feedback data, and a defense strategy based on provenance, versioning, access control, behavioral verification, and rollback.

caching-strategy.title: Caching Strategy and Distributed Cache Design
caching-strategy.summary: A strategy for designing caches from a consistency perspective — the layered structure that holds copies of slow origin data in a fast tier, the read/write paths (Cache-Aside, Write-Through/Back), LRU eviction, TTL/event-based invalidation, and handling distributed-cache failures such as stampede, penetration, and avalanche.

nist-csf-2.title: Cybersecurity Risk Management Based on the NIST Cybersecurity Framework 2.0
nist-csf-2.summary: An essay-style overview of NIST CSF 2.0 — its six functions (GOVERN, IDENTIFY, PROTECT, DETECT, RESPOND, RECOVER), the Core, Organizational Profile, and Implementation Tier structure, current-versus-target-state gap analysis, and cloud, AI, and supply-chain application strategy.

model-drift-monitoring.title: AI Model Drift and Data Drift Management
model-drift-monitoring.summary: An AI full-lifecycle strategy that distinguishes changes in inputs, ground truth, and predictions and performance degradation in the production environment as data, concept, and prediction drift, and manages them through baselines, statistical metrics, label delay, retraining, and rollback.

twelve-factor-app.title: The Twelve-Factor App
twelve-factor-app.summary: A SaaS design methodology that separates configuration, resources, and execution environment from code and designs processes to be stateless and disposable to ensure portability, scalability, and operational automation, inherited and extended by containers, Kubernetes, and serverless.

ml-model-registry.title: Machine Learning Model Registry and Approval/Deployment Governance
ml-model-registry.summary: A strategy that centrally manages machine learning models' versions, training runs, data and code lineage, evaluation, approval, and deployment pointers, and manages models as trustworthy operational assets through quality gates, canaries, rollback, audit, and supply-chain security.

synthetic-data.title: Synthetic Data
synthetic-data.summary: Artificially generated data that mimics the statistical properties of the original through rules, simulation, and generative models (GAN, VAE, Diffusion, LLM), enabling privacy protection, data augmentation, and reinforcement of sparse scenarios, while managing the fidelity, utility, and privacy trade-off through differential privacy and continuous verification.

strangler-fig-pattern.title: Legacy Modernization Based on the Strangler Fig Pattern
strangler-fig-pattern.summary: A strategy that lets legacy and new functionality coexist through a facade/routing layer and modernizes a large-scale system without downtime via business slices, data ownership, CDC, gradual traffic shifting, rollback, and observability, then removes the temporary structure and the legacy.

nfv.title: Network Functions Virtualization (NFV)
nfv.summary: A network cloudification technology that decouples network functions locked into dedicated hardware into software (VNFs) on general-purpose servers and automates the lifecycle with ETSI MANO (NFVO, VNFM, VIM) — evolving toward CNF, 5G, and edge.

digital-product-passport.title: Digital Product Passport (DPP)
digital-product-passport.summary: A product data architecture that combines unique identifiers for products, parts, and materials, data carriers, the EU Registry, decentralized detailed data, and access, evidence, and lifecycle governance to support sustainability, circularity, and regulatory compliance.

graph-database.title: Graph Databases and Property Graph/RDF Models
graph-database.summary: An explanation of the structure and modeling procedure of graph databases, which make nodes, relationships, and properties the core of their storage structure to query paths, patterns, and connectivity, along with the selection criteria between property graphs and RDF, applications in querying, analytics, fraud detection, and recommendation, and the boundaries of quality, security, and ledgers.

tsn.title: Time-Sensitive Networking (TSN)
tsn.summary: A set of deterministic Ethernet technologies that adds time synchronization (802.1AS), time-aware scheduling (802.1Qbv), lossless redundancy (802.1CB), and central configuration (802.1Qcc) on top of standard Ethernet to guarantee bounded latency and low jitter, covering the real-time communication foundation of IT/OT convergence, autonomous driving, and smart factories.

ai-model-card-dataset-datasheet.title: AI Transparency Based on AI Model Cards and Dataset Datasheets
ai-model-card-dataset-datasheet.summary: An overview of how to achieve AI transparency, accountability, change management, and operational control by linking model cards, which record an AI model's purpose, performance, limitations, and risks, and datasheets, which describe a dataset's provenance, composition, quality, and rights, with data lineage, the model registry, evaluation, and monitoring.

recommendation-system.title: Recommendation System
recommendation-system.summary: An information-filtering system that predicts and ranks items a user will prefer amid information overload — combining content-based, collaborative filtering, and hybrid (deep learning) approaches in a multi-stage pipeline of candidate generation, ranking, and re-ranking.

cobit-2019-governance.title: IT Governance Design and Implementation Based on COBIT 2019
cobit-2019-governance.summary: A study note that summarizes COBIT 2019's separation of governance and management, five domains, components, 11 design factors, target capability levels, and implementation and assurance procedures, along with finance, cloud, and AI examples.

recurrent-neural-network.title: Recurrent Neural Networks (RNN) and LSTM/GRU
recurrent-neural-network.summary: The structure, principles, and comparison of RNNs, which process variable-length sequences by recurrently passing past context through a hidden state, and of LSTM/GRU, which overcome vanishing gradients through gates and cell state to learn long-term dependencies, and the trade-offs versus Transformers and state-space models.

open-ran.title: Open RAN (Open Radio Access Network) Architecture and RIC-Based Intelligence
open-ran.summary: An overview of the structure, interfaces, deployment, performance, security, and multi-vendor operation strategy of Open RAN, which combines RU/DU/CU functional split, open interfaces, virtualization, and intelligent control based on SMO, Non-RT RIC, and Near-RT RIC.

data-space-architecture.title: Data Spaces and Data-Sovereignty-Based Trusted Data Sharing
data-space-architecture.summary: An overview of a federated data architecture that shares data across organizations while data providers retain control, by combining trust services, catalogs, semantics, contracts, and usage policies, along with its governance, security, and diffusion strategy.

mpls.title: MPLS (Multi-Protocol Label Switching)
mpls.summary: An L2.5 connection-oriented technology that attaches a 20-bit label to IP packets to traverse the core via exact-match switching — LER/LSP, FEC, label stacks, LDP/RSVP-TE/MP-BGP distribution, L3/L2 VPN, traffic engineering, FRR, and the evolution toward segment routing (SR-MPLS, SRv6).

microsegmentation.title: East-West Traffic Control and Zero Trust Implementation Based on Microsegmentation
microsegmentation.summary: A zero trust implementation means that divides east-west traffic among assets, workloads, and services into small logical boundaries based on business flows and identity, and enforces default-deny, least privilege, and continuous verification to reduce lateral movement and the blast radius after a breach.

test-driven-development.title: Test-Driven Development (TDD)
test-driven-development.summary: An evolutionary development technique that repeats short cycles of writing a failing test first (Red), passing it with a minimal implementation (Green), and improving the structure (Refactor) to simultaneously secure an executable specification, loosely coupled design, and a regression safety net. Extends to the FIRST principles, test doubles, the classicist/London schools, and BDD/ATDD integration.

spiffe-spire-workload-identity.title: SPIFFE/SPIRE-Based Workload Identity and Secretless Service Authentication
spiffe-spire-workload-identity.summary: A standard and operational framework that automatically issues SPIFFE IDs and short-lived SVIDs to dynamic services through node and workload attestation, and implements service authentication and least privilege without long-lived secrets via the Workload API, mTLS, and trust-domain federation.

idempotency.title: Idempotency Design and Distributed System Reliability
idempotency.summary: An overview of the definition of idempotency — whereby performing the same operation multiple times does not change the final state — its distinction from safety and atomicity, HTTP method conventions and delivery semantics, the implementation of idempotency keys, natural keys, and idempotent consumers with atomic reservation, payment and messaging examples, and integration with resilience patterns.

wifi-7.title: High-Performance, Low-Latency Wireless LAN Design Based on Wi-Fi 7 (IEEE 802.11be)
wifi-7.summary: A professional-engineer essay-style overview of Wi-Fi 7 based on IEEE 802.11be-2024 — the principles of 320 MHz channels, MLO, 4096-QAM, OFDMA, and Multi-RU, a comparison with Wi-Fi 6, 5G, and wired networks, and RF, backhaul, security, observability, and phased-adoption strategy.

kubernetes-gateway-api.title: Cloud-Native Traffic Management Based on the Kubernetes Gateway API
kubernetes-gateway-api.summary: A professional-engineer essay-style overview of the role-oriented resource model of GatewayClass, Gateway, HTTPRoute, and GRPCRoute, the controller and data-plane coordination principles, standardization, multi-protocol support, and cross-namespace trust compared to Ingress, and TLS, observability, canary, and gradual-migration strategy.

web-accessibility.title: Web Accessibility and WCAG/KWCAG
web-accessibility.summary: A professional-engineer essay-style overview of the quality attribute that ensures everyone, including people with disabilities and older adults, can use web information equally — the four POUR principles, WCAG 2.2 (international, AA) and KWCAG 2.2 (4 principles, 14 guidelines, 33 items), the accessibility-by-design process, automated, manual, and user evaluation, and WCAG 3.0 trends.
